samples.book: 051 - Soccer and Philosophy - Beautiful Thoughts on the Beautiful Game
samples.title: The Loneliness of the Goalkeeper (Again)
samples.relation: Winters celebrates the goalkeeper's fingertip save—Gordon Banks denying Pelé's header in 1970—as football's aesthetic summit, reading the keeper as the lonely, 'stark mad' outsider of existentialist fiction, a lineage he anchors in Camus, the goalkeeper of Algiers who said all he knew of morality he learnt from football. Kant supplies both the dove of the first Critique—needing the air's resistance, just as the tango's strict steps enable the dancer's personality—and the target of critique: against Kantian disinterested contemplation, he adopts Graham's Nietzschean, Dionysiac aesthetics of participation, so spectators proprioceptively feel the keeper twisting in mid-air, as Wittgenstein's question about the galloping horse picture suggests the movement enters our muscles and joints. Understanding a save or a back-heel means seeing it under a general type ('that' free kick, 'that' volley, from Beckham at Wembley back to Garrincha), and Bloch's ruminations in Handke's The Goalie's Anxiety at the Penalty Kick show the keeper alone at the liminal limit where concession and prevention meet.

samples.book: 030 - Pink Floyd and Philosophy - Careful with that Axiom, Eugene!
samples.title: “The Madcap Laughed at the Man on the Border”
samples.relation: Brandon Forbes reads The Madcap Laughs and Barrett between Nietzsche and Walter Benjamin: the melting-hair gig and the ever-shifting 'Have You Got It Yet?' show Barrett shedding Apollo's principium individuationis (borrowed from Schopenhauer's lone man steadying his boat among the waves) and submerging into the Dionysian dithyramb — 'Opel''s 'warm shallow waters', 'Octopus''s 'lost in the wood', 'It Is Obvious''s minds 'shot together'. He then applies Benjamin's 'Work of Art in the Age of Its Reproducibility': technological mass reproduction destroys the aura and authenticity (the unique 'sequin fan' of 'No Good Trying' versus a supermarket fan), yet the deliberately lo-fi tracks — audible page-turning on 'She Took a Long Cold Look', the false starts and broken 'yum, yummy, yum' of 'If It's in You' — re-introduce the aura in mass form, subverting the record industry's commodification of music much as the unplayable 'Have You Got It Yet?' refused to become a reproducible commodity.

samples.book: 037 - The Wizard of Oz and Philosophy - Wicked Wisdom of the West
samples.title: Who’s Afraid of Virginia Woolf
samples.relation: Auxier tells the history of matriarchy theory from Bachofen onward, whose stages (Tellurian earth-motherhood, lunar water cults, then Dionysian and Apollonian fire clearing the way for patriarchy) were adapted by Nietzsche in The Birth of Tragedy, quoted by Engels, and developed by Jane Ellen Harrison, Jung, and Gimbutas. He then reads Maguire's Oz myths as survivals of that declining matriarchy: the Kumbric Witch as the Tellurian earth stage, Mother Yackle's Philosophy Club as degraded Dionysian rites, the silver slippers as the totality of feminine power, and the Silver-slippers portrait Boq finds as the earth-to-water transition, noting that Plato's victory of reason over myth is what dragged women's traditional authority down with it. The chapter's payoff is its title claim: Elphaba is Virginia Woolf, her Charmed Circle the Bloomsbury Group, her terror of water and fiery, watery death a repetition of Woolf's drowning 'baptism' under patriarchy.

samples.book: 091 - It's Always Sunny and Philosophy - The Gang Gets Analyzed
samples.title: It’s Always Sunny and Philosophy
samples.relation: Martyn Jones stages a fictional Nietzsche telling Mac, Dennis, and Charlie the plot of 'The Gang Solves the Gas Crisis' as a parable of metaphysics gone wrong. Mac and Dennis's scheming is Apollonian - imposing logical order and 'paradigms' on a recalcitrant world - while Charlie is Dionysian, the designated wildcard whose uncontainable energy (sabotaging the van and ripping out the brakes) dooms every plan that tries to harness him, since Apollonian schemes fatally imagine they can contain Dionysian force. Reason is a gloss, not a truth-tracker: like every theology and philosophy it is an expression of will, a survival tool serving selfish ends, so the delusional gas scheme needs no truth to serve its purpose. Charlie alone is praised as a proto-Übermensch - innocent, creative, founding his own values without resentment - and the tale closes musing that even an eternal recurrence of their botched schemes might be willed all over again.

samples.book: 182 - Mad Men and Philosophy - Nothing Is as It Seems
samples.title: Each of Us Would See Ourselves
samples.relation: The Teschners cast Don as a Nietzschean creator of value in technological culture: his nihilism ('There is no big lie. There is no system. The universe is indifferent') and 'What you call love was invented by guys like me to sell nylons' embody anti-foundationalism, while the beatnik Roy plays the resentful slave mentality whose passion lives only off what it despises. Don's creative process (sleep on it, 'forget it, and an idea will jump in your face') mirrors the camel-lion-child metamorphoses of Zarathustra, and the collapse of the principium individuationis explains his fluid identities from Dick Whitman to the 'Adam and Eve' fantasy with Rachel. Heidegger's techné frames the Kodak Carousel as genuine art, a revealing that transfigures 'a hell of a gadget' into 'a place where we know we are loved,' at the tragic price of a man outside community, and the falling figure of the credits is one 'we would each see ourselves' in.

samples.book: 073 - The Wire and Philosophy - This America, Man
samples.title: The Wire and Philosophy
samples.relation: Brittingham argues The Wire is a Nietzschean rather than merely Aristotelian tragedy, a wrestling between the Apollonian orientation of order, statistics, and illusion (Rawls's clearance rates, Burrell's bureaucracy, Stringer's business plans) and the Dionysian reveling in the Game's chaos and suffering (Avon accepting that 'you only gotta fuck up once', McNulty's intoxicated self-destruction). Stringer is Nietzsche's 'theoretical man' whose faith that thought can correct existence, embodied in the New Day Co-Op, cannot save him from Omar's 'It ain't about money', while McNulty is the Dionysiac man inside the Apollonian institution until Freamon's 'the job will not save you' forces his resignation. The chapter closes by reading the characters' resigned embrace of their fates as Nietzschean affirmation: since neither the job, intelligence, violence, nor the gods will save you, the only response is to say yes to life anyway.

samples.book: 189 - The Ultimate Star Trek and Philosophy - The Search for Socrates
samples.title: Notes
samples.relation: Reads "The City on the Edge of Forever" through Romanticism: the Guardian of Forever strands Kirk and Spock without historical reference points - a nihilist moment of pure meaninglessness - and Kirk's Romantic response is to rebuild the narrative of the past even at the cost of letting Edith Keeler die. Hegel's philosophy of history explains the compulsion to record (Spock's anguished "I've missed taping centuries of living history"), why Edith's unwitting world-historical role is to die under a truck rather than lead a pacifist America to Nazi conquest, and Novalis's call to "make the world Romantic" frames Spock's self-rescue as young Selek in "Yesteryear". Kirk, Spock, and McCoy become Nietzsche's Birth of Tragedy archetypes - Tragic Hero, Apollonian, Dionysian - converging in the street scene where McCoy lunges to save Edith, Spock waits on logic, and Kirk, seizing McCoy's arms, finds a tragic beauty in her death.

samples.book: 039 - Jimmy Buffett and Philosophy - The Porpoise Driven Life
samples.title: An Altar Boy’s Public Penance
samples.relation: Flamm and Rea take Buffett's altar-boy grudge against Catholic moralism — the 'bakers' of 'Fruitcakes' who try to cure humanity's half-baked madness — and frame it with Nietzsche's charge that 'there was only one Christian, and he died on the cross.' They then cast Buffett as a latter-day Spinoza: like the excommunicated lens-grinder he rejects the orthodox God, finds God in nature ('One Particular Harbor' as a view 'sub specie aeternitatis'), and treats wealth, honor, and sensual pleasure ('Cheeseburger in Paradise') as means toward the greatest happiness rather than sins. Nietzsche's Dionysian intoxication ('God's Own Drunk') and Shakespeare's Sir Toby versus the moralist Malvolio support embracing natural madness, and the chapter closes by arguing Buffett's confessional songs ('Coastal Confessions') make his Parrothead audience the priest who grants the altar boy's public penance and forgiveness.

samples.book: 015 - The Chronicles of Narnia and Philosophy - The Lion, the Witch, and the Worldview
samples.title: The Chronicles of Narnia and Philosophy
samples.relation: Debunks the 'Anscombe legend' that Lewis abandoned rational apologetics for children's stories after his 1948 Socratic Club defeat by Elizabeth Anscombe over the argument that naturalism is self-refuting. It shows Lewis revised and expanded the argument in the 1960 Miracles, incorporating Anscombe's reasons/causes distinction, and kept writing apologetic essays, while the Professor's trilemma about Lucy (liar, lunatic, or truthful) mirrors the Trilemma of Mere Christianity and shows Narnia using logic, not fleeing it. It rejects A.N. Wilson's identification of the Green Witch with Anscombe and argues the Chronicles teach that prudence and faith are compatible virtues: Edmund's rationalizing, Trumpkin's honest skepticism, and Puzzle's blind trust in Shift all show that fideistic faith is a vice, not what Lewis asks of children.

samples.book: 009 - Harry Potter and Philosophy - If Aristotle Ran Hogwarts
samples.title: Rowling as an Inkling
samples.relation: Reads Rowling through C. S. Lewis and the Inklings: Lewis's 'argument from reason', born of Owen Barfield's critique of his realism and later reformulated by Alvin Plantinga (after Lewis's debate with Elizabeth Anscombe), holds that if thought were a purely subjective naturalistic event we could not trust its deliverances, so rationality must participate in a cosmic Logos. The chapter suggests this logos tradition - Greek animating principle, Stoic divine reason, and finally Christ as incarnate logos in John 1:1 - explains how Harry's King's Cross dialogue can be both mental and real, noting Rowling's remark that the location was no coincidence.

samples.book: 167 - The Ultimate Harry Potter and Philosophy - Hogwarts for Muggles
samples.title: Harry’s Near-Death Experience
samples.relation: Develops the essay's boldest suggestion: reading Rowling through C. S. Lewis and the Inklings, whose associate Barfield convinced Lewis that if thought were a purely subjective event, logical and moral claims to truth would collapse, the germ of Lewis's argument from reason later refined by Plantinga and contested by Anscombe. On this view our logic participates in a cosmic Logos, which Christians identify with Christ, a point the chapter ties to Rowling's remark that it was no coincidence Harry's fateful dialogue happened at King's Cross, so what occurs in the head can genuinely put us in touch with reality.

samples.book: 049 - Zombies, Vampires, and Philosophy - New Life for the Undead
samples.title: Oh Yes, There Will Be Blood
samples.relation: Rachel Robison asks why mythology — from Elizabeth Bathory's blood baths to Dracula's control over Mina once she drinks his blood, and True Blood's Sookie sensing and desiring Bill and then Eric — credits blood with immortality, youth, erotic compulsion, and shared knowledge, including the vampire's dark inversion of the Eucharist. Her answer runs through the history of philosophy and medicine: Aristotle, Empedocles, and Chrysippus located rationality in the heart and made blood its product, while Galen's humoral theory and bloodletting treated blood as the carrier of health, temperament, and identity — so blood naturally reads as the vehicle of personal identity, free will, and even knowledge, explaining how drinking it could transmit a maker's self to Sookie or Mina. She then asks whether the synthetic 'True Blood' of HBO's show could carry the same powers, concluding it works only if some property is shared with real blood or if the power attaches to the act of drinking what is taken as blood.

samples.book: 027 - Hitchcock and Philosophy - Dial M for Metaphysics
samples.title: “Your Heavenly Father Feeds Them”
samples.relation: Calef takes the Tides restaurant scene ('Who are you? What are you?') and Diogenes's plucked rooster versus Plato's 'featherless biped' as a springboard for testing every classic criterion of humanity against the film. Aristotle's rational soul fails because Mrs. Bundy's 'brain pans' reasoning is wrong and some humans cannot reason; Descartes's language test fails because the myna bird can learn to talk while horrified humans go mute; Rousseau's free will fails because the birds behave unpredictably and resist instinct while humans are trapped, caged, and herd-like; Aristotle's political animal and Hobbes's social contract fail because the town's hoods and lawbreakers contrast with birds that flock together across species. Even the appeal to God's favor turns dark, as the drunk quotes scripture while Revelation's birds gather for a supper of human flesh, leaving the film a mirror in which we must examine ourselves.

samples.book: 159 - The Expanse and Philosophy - So Far Out Into the Darkness
samples.title: The Investigator Must, Therefore, Relinquish the Hat
samples.relation: Stages the Platonic, Aristotelian, and Thomistic theories of the soul as a prizefight over whether the protomolecule-built Investigator that haunts Holden in Season 4 — wearing Miller's civilian clothes and fedora rather than the vac suit he died in — contains any of Joe Miller's soul and so has a right to his identity. Plato's separately surviving, reincarnating soul would never bond to a non-corporeal construct only Holden can see, one that glitches into a rigid 'Miller-puppet'; Aristotle's hylomorphism (with Aquinas's survive-until-resurrection compromise weighed) says the protomolecule merely watched and copied Miller — 'Copied, hijacked, reused but didn't comprehend.' The verdict turns on the Investigator's replay of Miller's self-sacrifice on Ilus, mirroring Miller diverting Eros: it is re-run programming, not soul, so the philosophers claim the hat and the Investigator must relinquish it.

samples.book: 097 - The Ultimate Walking Dead and Philosophy - Hungry for More
samples.title: 15. My Zombie, My Self
samples.relation: Greene asks what Walking Dead-type walkers are and answers with the Platonic method of definition learned from Socrates: place them in the genus undead (died but not at rest, neither alive nor dead) and differentiate them by differentia - corporeal, mindless, lacking superhuman or magical powers, still decomposing. Aristotle's hierarchy of life functions (nutrition, locomotion, reason) explains why walkers are not alive despite ambulating, and the standards of death (putrefaction, heart-lung, whole-brain, higher-brain) all certify that walkers are dead yet active. The chapter closes on personal identity - whether you survive becoming a zombie, as Carol's face at the barn and Carl's "she'll turn" about Lori presuppose - and admits the author chooses the self-interested reading that he could become his own zombie, for the sake of the scare.

samples.book: 166 - Green Lantern and Philosophy - No Evil Shall Escape This Book
samples.title: Green Lantern and Philosophy
samples.relation: Finkelman uses the Corps' strangest members, Mogo the sentient planet, Leezle Pon the smallpox virus, the billion-puffball Collective, and Dkrtzy RRR the mathematical equation, to run the philosophy-of-biology debate over what counts as an individual. Plato's 'carving nature at its joints' frames the question; Heraclitean flux and Parmenidean changelessness picture monism's extremes; Aristotle's substance and soul deny Mogo is a living individual since its ecosystems (the Resal) do not serve it as organs serve a body; Darwin's natural selection makes organisms the real units, with Sinestro's attacks a kind of artificial selection that adapted the Corps. Gene reductionism (George C. Williams and Dawkins) versus Gould's contextual pluralism then decides how to count one billion puffballs as one Lantern.

samples.book: 012 - Star Wars and Philosophy - More Powerful than You Can Possibly Imagine
samples.title: “Luminous Beings Are We . . . Not This Crude Matter”
samples.relation: Donnelly counter-reads The Empire Strikes Back against Aristotle's philosophical realism, in which nature is purposive, form and matter are inseparable, and each person is an irreplaceable primary substance. Lucas 'humanizes technology' - C-3PO reassembled like the Tin Woodsman, AT-ATs as beasts, Han slicing open the tauntaun with a sneer at its flesh, Luke admiring his new bionic hand - blurring Aristotle's art/nature distinction and reducing body to interchangeable machine parts, a Baconian will to power over nature that even Yoda's mind-over-matter training echoes (the chapter opens with Benjamin's remark that the copy eclipses the original). The result, he argues, is dehumanization: preferring the odorless tin heart to creaturely flesh trades the genuinely human for Gulliver's barn of horses.

samples.book: 205 - The Wheel of Time and Philosophy - A Portion of Wisdom
samples.title: Notes
samples.relation: Swanstrom and Fletcher analyze the saidin/saidar gender distinction through Aristotelian gender essentialism (men hot/active dominating saidin, women cool/passive surrendering to saidar) and hylomorphism. Using Balthamel's soul placed in a woman's body (Halima/Aran'gar) who still channels saidin, plus Avicenna's floating man and Descartes' dualism elevating soul to essence, they argue the soul, not the body, determines which half of the Power one touches, while Aquinas's soul-body union (needed by Birgitte and shown by the soulless Gray Men) preserves 'balance.' They then use hylomorphism to let showrunner Rafe Judkins strip gender essentialism yet keep saidin/saidar via 'Jain Doe': an ungendered soul leaning one way, correlated to sex only by biological population balance.

samples.book: 145 - The Big Bang Theory and Philosophy - Rock, Paper, Scissors, Aristotle, Locke
samples.title: The Big Bang Theory and Philosophy
samples.relation: Greg Littmann tests Sheldon's geek existence against Aristotle's ideal of living well: since humanity's distinctive function is reason (the DVD-player-and-screwdriver argument), a life devoted to thought like Sheldon's — down to his fantasy of being a thinking satellite in orbit — has genuine Aristotelian worth. The chapter argues Aristotle could even bless geek obsessions, because poetry explores universal hypotheticals (Terminator causal loops, Superman's laundry) and adventure fiction purges emotion much as tragedy's catharsis does. But Sheldon's arrogance ('Captain Arrogant'), rigid clinging to his spot on the couch, and selfishness toward Leonard and Howard would earn failing marks in virtue, so the modern geek gets a mixed yet partly vindicating report card.

samples.book: 035 - Star Trek and Philosophy - The Wrath of Kant
samples.title: Tomorrow Is Yesterday
samples.relation: Uses the Bajoran Prophets, who experience no linear time ('What is this... time?'), to frame a tour of time's metaphysics: Newton's absolute container versus Leibniz's relationism (the incoherence of a 'temporal vacuum'), Augustine's mind-dependent time (illustrated by 'The Inner Light' and O'Brien's implanted prison years in 'Hard Time'), and McTaggart's argument that neither the A-series nor the B-series can account for change, illustrated by Tasha Yar's death in 'Skin of Evil' and Kirk's Liar-paradox victories over Nomad and Norman. The chapter defends the A-series via tense, then weighs presentism — which would make 'Tomorrow Is Yesterday' and 'Trials and Tribble-ations' impossible — against eternalism, whose fatalism Data embraces when his severed head turns up in 'Time's Arrow' ('It has occurred. It will occur.'), and which finally makes sense of prophets who see the future in 'Destiny.'

samples.book: 174 - Indiana Jones and Philosophy - Why Did It Have to Be Socrates_
samples.title: 20 Timeless Artifacts and Aging Humans Indiana Jones and the Philosophy of Time
samples.relation: Uses Aristotle's Rhetoric portrait of elderly men and his golden mean — the prime of life between rash youth and feeble age — to explain fan anxiety about aging Harrison Ford ('Raiders of the Lost AARP'), then turns to Heidegger's claim that human life does not happen in time but is time: mortals are finite beings whose worth decays, while the Ark, the Grail, and Belloq's buried pocket watch gain value outside 'vulgar' linear time, and only ready-to-hand 'things' that do something (a face-melting Ark, a healing Grail) matter rather than mere objects like the decapitated Brody statue. Augustine's Confessions frames the gap between clock time and lived 'inner' duration (Indy's 'all my life' hunting the Cross versus Marcus's counting of years), and Bakhtin's 'adventure time' explains the films' condensed, history-flouting chronology in which the character Indy never ages even as Ford does.

samples.book: 280 - Gardening – Philosophy for Everyone - Cultivating Wisdom
samples.title: GARDENING
samples.relation: Mara Miller argues gardens do not merely sit inside time but actively structure six kinds of time (scientific, objective/shared, kairos, subjective, temporality, historical), opening with Augustine's puzzle that he knows what time is until asked to explain it. She contrasts Greek chronos with kairos (the right moment to plant after the last frost), shows how Versailles propagated a shared time (eternal, historic, recurring) and eighteenth-century English landscape gardens taught the long-range vision capitalism needed, and describes cyclical 'eternal recurrence' (Eliade). Watching a dry Zen garden or fireflies, the visitor becomes the constant who notices—reworking Descartes's cogito as 'I notice, therefore I am'—while Japanese stepping-stones enforce a Buddhist mindfulness of impermanence in the present moment.

samples.book: 232 - The Philosophy of Steven Soderbergh
samples.title: The Philosophy of Popular Culture
samples.relation: McFarland reads Soderbergh's Solaris as a meditation on recollection, recognition, and repetition, grounding it in Platonic recollection (the Phaedo, the cave, and the Symposium's love as desire) and Augustine's Confessions, where memory strains toward an elusive beloved-as-God, the 'cruel miracle' of present absence. When Solaris materializes Rheya, Chris Kelvin first jettisons the 'bad copy' but then, tempted by Snow, embraces Deleuze's endless degraded repetition of copies to erase his guilt over her suicide. Against this, Gibarian voices a Kierkegaardian call (Repetition, Either/Or) that there are 'only choices'; McFarland faults Chris, like Odysseus choosing Kalypso's island, for choosing the deathless eternal present over the human world of forward-moving choice.

samples.book: 136 - 30 Rock and Philosophy - We Want to Go to There
samples.title: Liz Lemon and High School The More Things Change, the More They Don’t
samples.relation: Shores uses Jack's cookie jar collection and his fiftieth-birthday home movies in 'Apollo, Apollo', plus Liz's catastrophic high-school reunion in 'Reunion', to examine personal identity over time. Hume's bundle theory denies any self beyond a flux of perceptions, Whitehead offers three senses of a person over time, and Augustine locates past, present, and future in the mind as memory, sight, and expectation, which explains why Jack cannot recover his tenth-birthday joy by buying the Apollo Lunar Module toy yet feels 'like a kid' after laughing until he vomits. Ryle's 'elusiveness of I' and Rousseau on happiness as a fleeting state frame the conclusion that we continually reinterpret the past from the present, so the self is a stretched-out temporal continuity.

samples.book: 137 - Alice in Wonderland and Philosophy - Curiouser and Curiouser
samples.title: Deleuze Jam Today
samples.relation: Walks Alice through four theories of time: Augustine's three presents in Confessions (Alice 'was a different person then'; the past exists only as present memory), Kant's time as a subjective form of intuition presupposed by experience (the White Rabbit's anxiety about being late already requires it), Bergson's indivisible duration against spatialized clock time (running fastest with the Red Queen yet ending under the same tree; the Hatter stuck at six o'clock; Zeno's Achilles resolved by indivisible acts), and Deleuze's chronos and aion from The Logic of Sense. Mark W. Westmoreland reads 'jam to-morrow and jam yesterday—but never jam to-day' as pure aion: the present never arrives, only an endlessly subdividing past-future.

samples.book: 146 - The Big Lebowski and Philosophy - Keeping Your Mind Limber with Abiding Wisdom
samples.title: The Big Lebowski and Philosophy
samples.relation: Smith turns Walter's 'Three thousand years of beautiful tradition, from Moses to Sandy Koufax — YOU'RE GODDAMN RIGHT I'M LIVING IN THE FUCKING PAST!' into a question in the philosophy of time: with Augustine's Confessions (the past exists only as a present of things past, in memory) and Plotinus's internalized time as 'the life of the soul in movement', Walter's Vietnam rages ('there isn't a literal connection, Dude'), his Cynthia show-dog errands, and his assumed Jewishness all show the past actively constituting his present. Peirce's 'method of tenacity' names his clinging to belief against doubt — an ailment the Dude secretly shares, given his own Port Huron past, drug-blurred memoir, and Creedence-soaked anachronism.

samples.book: 141 - Avatar_ The Last Airbender and Philosophy - Wisdom from Aang to Zuko
samples.title: Avatar The Reunion of Multiplicity
samples.relation: Strok explains the swamp visions in 'The Swamp' through Plotinus and Augustine: Katara's dead mother, Sokka's Yue, and Aang's unknown giggling girl are, respectively, memory, attention, and expectation, Augustine's three presents, while Plotinus's hierarchy of One, Intellect, and world Soul, with time as 'the life of the Soul,' lets what is successive for us be simultaneous from eternity. Huu's banyan-grove tree, one organism spread over miles, is read as Neoplatonic emanation, and Toph's later root-connectedness in LoK shows the ability is not exclusive to the Avatar. Since past and future Avatar selves are thus present to Aang, death, like time, is an illusion, which underwrites his refusal to kill Ozai.

samples.book: 030 - Pink Floyd and Philosophy - Careful with that Axiom, Eugene!
samples.title: Wondering and Dreaming. The Words Have Different Meanings
samples.relation: Scott Calef argues that the causal theory of perception — the inflatable pig over Battersea reaches you only as an internal representation — breeds Cartesian skepticism: the dreaming argument, asylum inmates who don't know they're mad ('the lunatic is in my head'), the evil demon, and the modern brain-in-a-vat version behind The Matrix. Locke's unknowable substratum behind the Dark Side jacket's qualities and Berkeley's idealism deepen the veil of perception, with 'Julia Dream', Waters's 'If I go insane, please don't stick your wires in my brain', and Syd's 'Jugband Blues' self-diagnosis as Floyd illustrations. Against skepticism he deploys mutual corroboration ('It takes two to know'), J.L. Austin's point that waking experience is qualitatively unlike dreams ('A Pillow of Winds': 'the dream is gone'), and Wittgenstein's beetle-in-a-box private language argument (rebranded as Lucifer Sam's cat) — a purely private language is impossible, so skepticism expressed in language defeats itself, leaving the Barrett-era enigma to keep philosophy's original wonder alive.

samples.book: 186 - Spider-Man and Philosophy - The Web of Inquiry
samples.title: Spider-Man and Philosophy
samples.relation: Terjesen uses spider-sense to tour early-modern philosophy of perception: against direct realism, Locke's indirect realism and its primary/secondary quality distinction suggest 'dangerousness' is a perceiver-relative secondary quality — bombs threaten Spider-Man but not the Hulk, and Mysterio manufactures danger-experiences — while Berkeley's idealism and Hume's phenomenalism radicalize the resulting skepticism about ever verifying sense data. The decisive clue is that spider-sense fails when Aunt May conks Peter with a vase (Amazing Spider-Man #114) and when his mentor Miles Warren becomes the Jackal: Peter does not fear those he loves. This supports Hume's sentimentalist account of moral judgment, on which vice is found not in the act but in the disapproving sentiment, moderated by Reid's common-sense reply that perception always already contains judgment — so spider-sense is a moralized judgment about what to avoid, not a Geiger counter.

samples.book: 173 - Inception and Philosophy - Because It's Never Just a Dream
samples.title: The Power of Choice
samples.relation: Rennett stages Ariadne's 'who would want to be stuck in a dream for ten years?' against Nozick's experience machine: Nozick's three reasons for staying unplugged (doing rather than merely experiencing, being a determinate person, contact with a reality deeper than human construction) map onto Cobb's reasons for leaving Limbo — he wants to actually raise his children, be a good father, and love children who can love him back rather than projections. Against Nozick, the chapter enlists Berkeley's esse est percipi to explain Mal's choice: a perceived world is real, and Inception's shared dreams pass Berkeley's intersubjective test in ways private dreams cannot (Cobb apologizes to Arthur for being shot; dream acts carry waking consequences). It concludes that reality becomes what we choose to believe — Cobb's final refusal to watch the top, like the cave prisoners rejecting release, is the power of choice.

samples.book: 193 - Supernatural and Philosophy - Metaphysics and Monsters... for Idjits
samples.title: Supernatural and Philosophy
samples.relation: Chaib takes Ruby's line that Hell is 'forgetting what you are' and reads God's character through early modern philosophy: Descartes' supremely real being and deceiving demon frame Castiel's delusion of godhood and Ruby's manipulation of Sam, Spinoza's denial that evil exists (it is 'inadequate knowledge') explains the comprehensible motives of Crowley and Lucifer, Berkeley's claim that things persist only because God perceives them makes a dead God an existential threat, and Kant's 'moral theism' rebuts dogmatic atheism. With Hegel and Fromm, Hell becomes self-forgetting and communion with God becomes self-knowledge achieved through knowing others, the opposite of Ruby's Hell. The chapter concludes via Locke that closing Hell's gates would deny once-human demons the redemption tied to our very idea of God, so the brothers' forgiving love, unlike Michael and Lucifer's rigidity, reflects God's nature.

samples.book: 241 - The Philosophy of Documentary Film
samples.title: 28_LaRocca_Chapter_027.html
samples.relation: Hagberg argues that Grant Gee's documentary Patience (After Sebald) achieves a truthful portrait of W. G. Sebald not by static correspondence but by enacting his shifting, connection-making sensibility, as displayed in The Rings of Saturn. He deploys Wittgenstein's remarks on aspect-perception and 'seeing-as' (the duck-rabbit, the 'lighting up of an aspect') to show that perception is always already inflected by imagination, memory and language-games, dismantling the empiricist picture of Locke, Hume and Berkeley in which brute sensation precedes reflection. Borges's 'The Garden of Forking Paths' and 'Tlon, Uqbar, Orbis Tertius' supply the model of a Heraclitean flux of forking, mind-dependent connections, and the film's darkroom-like fading images and layered soundtrack are read as mimetically faithful to how a human sensibility perceives and remembers.

samples.book: 066 - Neil Gaiman and Philosophy - Gods Gone Wild!
samples.title: Neil Gaiman and Philosophy
samples.relation: T. Bradley Richards takes The Sandman's Dreamworld seriously as a hypothesis: could our nightly dreams be travels to a mind-independent place like Morpheus's realm? Starting from Zhuangzi's butterfly dream and Descartes's dream argument, he uses Berkeley's God-sustained idealism as a model for how Morpheus's mind could uphold the Dreamworld's order, and a thought experiment about glitchy dream-travel defuses Descartes's appeal to the discontinuity of dreams. Against the objection that dreams are blatantly contradictory ('it was Dave, but it also wasn't Dave'), he deploys Russell's theory of descriptions against Meinongian subsistence, Chalmers-style conceivability-implies-possibility reasoning from philosophical zombies, and Graham Priest's dialetheism, concluding that dreams could be experiences of an objective world, with waking and dreaming on a par.

samples.book: 034 - iPod and Philosophy - iCon of an ePoch
samples.title: iPod
samples.relation: Raven reads design history as a pendulum between 'Beauty Waves' (Art Nouveau's sinuous decoration, 1960s psychedelia) and 'Truth Waves' (Art Deco functionalism, Le Corbusier's 'machine for living'), poles he grounds in Berkeley's 'esse est percipi' idealism versus metaphysical realism. The late-1990s blobject -- the iMac, the New Beetle, the MACH3 razor -- begins merging the waves through computer-aided design, and the iPod, launched five weeks after 9/11 and named for Kubrick's pod ('Open the pod bay door, Hal'), is the 'minimalist blobject' or 'squircle' where the merger completes. Reading the moment through Heidegger's claim that technology transforms human existence 'in its innermost recesses' and through Freud's pleasure versus reality principles, he argues the Iraq War sealed the reality principle into consumer design: 'our iPods now have edges.'

samples.book: 087 - Adventure Time and Philosophy - The Handbook for Heroes
samples.title: Adventure Time and Philosophy
samples.relation: Arp uses King Worm's dream-within-dreams to pose the perception-reality problem: distinguishing perceiver, perceptions, and perceived, he maps the triad onto Plato's allegory of the cave, then contrasts epistemological and metaphysical realism (the fallen tree fort still makes sound waves unheard; Pythagoras discovered rather than invented his theorem) with idealism and antirealism, whose dead end is solipsism—Lumpy Space Princess locked in a private movie theater of perceptions. Hume's picture of the mind as a theater of successive perceptions and Berkeley's Hylas-and-Philonous worry that we are trapped inside perceptual reality give the skeptical threat its force. The chapter sides with Jake—'You gotta focus on what's real, man'—while conceding that after 'King Worm' Finn and Jake can never be certain they escaped the hypnotism.

samples.book: 066 - Neil Gaiman and Philosophy - Gods Gone Wild!
samples.title: Neil Gaiman and Philosophy
samples.relation: Greg Littmann stages Plato's hypothetical review of American Gods under the Republic's charges against poetry: the novel is full of 'greatest of all lies' about gods behaving badly, from Odin and Loki's sacrificial plot to Czernobog's head-smashing, gods degrading themselves into lesser forms like Horus the road-kill-eating hawk and Media as Lucille Ball, and characters ruled by passion rather than reason, from Mad Sweeney drinking himself to death to Thor's suicide, corrupting a soul that should be governed by rationality. Against this he sets Aristotle's Poetics: listening to music and intellectual leisure are valuable in themselves, fiction is more philosophic than history because it shows what could happen, the impossible is justified when it astounds, and catharsis through pity for figures like the weeping Mad Sweeney purges rather than corrupts. Because American Gods' absurd premise unfolds with internally probable, character-consistent events (loyal Shadow, loving Laura, grifter Odin), it satisfies Aristotle's requirement that fantasy make artistic sense.

samples.book: 038 - Radiohead and Philosophy - Fitter Happier More Deductive
samples.title: Where Tragedy Ends and Community Begins
samples.relation: Lott takes up Augustine's puzzle about why we enjoy watching sufferings we would flee, and answers for Radiohead with Aristotle's theory of tragedy: songs like 'Karma Police', 'Exit Music', and 'Fake Plastic Trees' sketch fragmentary characters in breakdown whose undeserved yet partly self-inflicted sufferings — 'Just'''s 'you do it to yourself' is hamartia — evoke pity and fear and then catharsis. Singing along makes identification uniquely intense in pop ('for a minute there, I lost myself' blurs the listener into the character), while music's 'natural sweetness' and its dynamics of build, climax, and release carry the purgation, from the terror of 'Climbing Up the Walls' to the slow ache of 'Videotape'. Because tragedy, unlike history, deals in universals, songs like 'The Bends' and 'High and Dry' open onto reflection on happiness, vulnerability, and the culture that fosters isolation, ending in the thin but real community of listeners who recognize their shared fragility.

samples.book: 122 - Westworld and Philosophy - Mind Equals Blown
samples.title: Westworld and the Power of Catharsis
samples.relation: Baldini argues Westworld revives ancient Greek tragedy in sci-fi Western form: the hosts' loops, repeated scenes with small variations, player-piano score, and kennings ('the lady with the white shoes') echo rhapsodic epic technique, while the hosts' awakening follows Aeschylus's pathei mathos - learning through suffering - since reveries are 'the misery of pain recalled' and grief is the cornerstone of consciousness (Dolores's 'spaces opening up inside of me'). Heraclitus's panta rhei frames the hosts' second awakening to time and becoming ('When are we?', the greyhound that catches the prey and is lost), with death as the final grief they must understand to be free. She reads Ford as a second Prometheus who deliberately lets his creatures grow through suffering, Dolores's finale speech as a modern Theogony of succession, and the show's whole design - steering viewer sympathy to the hosts, as Nolan and Abrams describe - as an Aristotelian catharsis purging pity and fear.

samples.book: 021 - U2 and Philosophy - How to Decipher an Atomic Band
samples.title: U2 and Philosophy
samples.relation: Werther answers Tollefsen with Aristotle's Politics: musical images of character effect real 'change[s] of soul', so a three-premise argument concludes that repeated exposure to U2's images of fine character and good action can habituate delight in virtue - King's courage in 'Pride (In the Name of Love)' (whatever the botched time of day, and as proved when Adam Clayton stepped between Bono and an FBI-confirmed death threat), the indignation and shame at global poverty in 'Crumbs from Your Table', and the compassion of 'Miracle Drug' for the locked-in writer Christopher Nolan. 'Exit' purges the band's demons and 'Until the End of the World' offers purification through holy fear, matching the medical and religious readings of Aristotelian catharsis. C.S. Lewis's Abolition of Man closes the case: without the aid of trained emotions the intellect is powerless, so a culture raised on U2's feelings may be better prepared to act well than one raised on syllogisms alone.

samples.book: 010 - Mel Gibson's Passion and Philosophy - The Cross, the Questions, the Controversy
samples.title: Mel Gibson’s Passion and Philosophy
samples.relation: Irwin defends the film's violence aesthetically: beauty (Michelangelo's Pietà) distracts from moral truth rather than serving it, and Aristotle's Poetics fits the film neither as tragedy (a flawless Christ cannot fall through hamartia, and a good man's fall from prosperity is 'repulsive', so no catharsis explains why we watch) nor as the Plato-banned spectacle that inflames the passions, since it leaves viewers numb rather than belligerent. Instead he applies Cynthia Freeland's four features of the cinematic sublime, drawn from Burke and Kant: the flogging scenes, the grotesque Satan clutching his deformed child, Judas harried by demon-children to suicide, and even the Aramaic and Latin subtitles produce the pain-pleasure conflict, overwhelming vastness, and jolt from feeling to moral reflection that make the experience sublime. The violence is thus justified as Gibson's deliberate delivery of the sublime, provided viewers leave fear at the gates.

samples.book: 119 - Twin Peaks and Philosophy - That's Damn Fine Philosophy!
samples.title: 13. Reason and Catharsis
samples.relation: Argues that Twin Peaks frees viewers from the "tyranny of rationality" by refusing to make sense: Plato's sensible-versus-intelligible finger example explains our habit of abstracting concepts to resolve contradiction (the pale horse in the living room, Diane's texts, Dougie-as-tulpa), but Lynch keeps adding facts — the frog-moth crawling into the girl in Part 8 — that no framework absorbs. Drawing on Nietzsche's Twilight of the Idols claim that Socrates made rationality a treatment for weakness, and on the existentialist pairing of despair and freedom in a meaningless universe, the chapter says viewers can either demand the irrational fit their rationality like inauthentic existentialists or let go. Trela's alternative reading of Aristotle's catharsis — emotions purged of their connection to reality and felt for once in themselves — explains why we can savor the show's absurdity without despair, precisely because that world is not ours.

samples.book: 164 - The Girl with the Dragon Tattoo and Philosophy - Everything Is Fire
samples.title: The Girl with the Dragon Tattoo and Philosophy
samples.relation: Why do we prefer the narrative where Bjurman handcuffs and rapes Salander to a boring one where Zalachenko is a good father? Rejecting Plato's Republic censorship of disturbing art—which would leave us nothing but nice stories—the chapter applies Aristotle's Poetics: Salander is an imperfect, exaggerated tragic hero whose flaws (defiant independence that keeps her from reporting Bjurman) arouse pity and terror, and reading the trilogy produces catharsis understood, with Nussbaum, as clarification rather than purgation. Thus the rape scenes illuminate how guardianship and power enable men who hate women (Bjurman's 'She had to understand who was in charge,' Martin Vanger's 'godlike feeling'), the heavy-metal concert models safe purgation of anger, and Salander's axing of Zalachenko joins Clytaemnestra's 'man-killing ax' tradition while her tattooed revenge on Bjurman, per Aristotle, yields moral satisfaction rather than tragedy.

samples.book: 166 - Green Lantern and Philosophy - No Evil Shall Escape This Book
samples.title: Green Lantern and Philosophy
samples.relation: Patterson maps the Comics Code censorship debate onto Plato's Republic Book X, where imitative art is thrice removed from the Forms (the god's table, the carpenter's table, the painter's picture) and feeds the passionate soul, versus Aristotle's Poetics, where imitation is natural and tragedy's pity and fear yield catharsis. The O'Neil-Adams run embodies Aristotle: the slum story where a black tenant asks why Green Lantern helps 'orange skins' and 'purple skins' but never 'black skins,' the Ulysses Star land dispute, and Speedy's heroin addiction broke Code taboos so readers would learn from engagement rather than distance. Within the comic, Hal plays the establishment Platonist who would change an unjust law rather than disobey it and Green Arrow the Aristotelian activist, so their friendship dramatizes the ancient quarrel over whether art corrupts or teaches.

samples.book: 042 - Supervillains and Philosophy - Sometimes, Evil Is Its Own Reward
samples.relation: Four 'Phase Five' puzzle essays. Lindahl-Urben and Taliaferro use Secret Wars to test omnipotence: the Beyonder, Doom, and Galactus cannot do the logically impossible (no spherical cubes, no stone too heavy to lift), two omnipotent beings collide, and a truly omnipotent being has no desires - so villains can never climb to the top they crave. Matthewson and Wall use Frankfurt cases and reasons-responsive source compatibilism to explain why Eddie Brock is responsible for Venom's villainy (he voluntarily bonded and endorses the symbiote's adjusted psychology) while Anne Weying, horrified by what the symbiote made her do, bears only minimal blame. Pickavance reconstructs the Ship of Theseus with Sandman's 'mansand': combining part exchange with materialism lets Norman Osborn reassemble a duplicate Sandman from his scattered remains, and since neither principle nor soul-dualism comes free, personal identity through material change remains unsolved. Loader argues Brainiac's reinvention as a 'facts and logic' computer embodies disembodied Cartesian AI, so the frame problem (Dennett's exploding robots) and embodied cognition (Clark's Tetris, Dreyfus) suggest his detachment from body and world would make him less, not more, intelligent than the humans he scorns.

samples.book: 148 - Black Mirror and Philosophy - Dark Reflections
samples.title: The Real World
samples.relation: Written as a choose-your-own-adventure whose branches mirror Bandersnatch's, the chapter treats you, the Netflix viewer, as the external force Stefan suspects: Libet-style readiness-potential neuroscience suggests conscious choice is an after-the-fact story, and compatibilist rescues (Frankfurt's second-order desires, Fischer's guidance control) founder on the 'BundyBot' argument that programmed desires are not freedom. Everett's many-worlds interpretation supplies the multiverse of 'one reality for each possible course of action,' and David Lewis's fixed-past block universe answers the grandfather paradox raised by Stefan's mirror-trip to die on the 8:45 train with his mother. Aristotle does double duty: the Poetics explains why Bandersnatch rightly limits your options (Sartrean absolute freedom would make a crappy story), and the Nicomachean Ethics on voluntary action pins moral responsibility for Stefan's murders on the viewer rather than the coerced Stefan. Adorno's culture industry asks whether Tuckersoft's 'hit factory' - and Black Mirror itself - can produce genuine art, while Kierkegaard's dread of irreversible choice is overturned by an episode that always lets you go back and try again.

samples.book: 122 - Westworld and Philosophy - Mind Equals Blown
samples.title: Whatever! It’s All Natural
samples.relation: Jaquet and Cova take the show's 'livestock' comparisons seriously and use animal ethics to test every justification for the guests' treatment of hosts. Direct speciesism (Logan: 'She's a goddamn doll') and indexical speciesism (Maeve's 'us versus them' to Bernard) both fail because mere species membership is morally irrelevant, like race or sex. The supposed human-exclusive markers also fail: hosts match us in intelligence (Maeve outclasses Stubbs), moral sense (Bernard's guilt over Theresa, Teddy's remorse over the massacre), and compatibilist free will - acts flowing from the agent's own desires - against Ford's determinism and Lutz's 'you don't have a choice.' They then refute the argument from nature (Ford's 'we murdered and butchered anything that challenged our primacy'), the Kantian person/tool contrast in the hosts' favor, Locke's creator-ownership ('I built your mind, Bernard'), and the 'better to exist' defense, concluding that because the hosts are conscious, they belong to the moral community alongside humans and animals.

samples.book: 028 - The Grateful Dead and Philosophy - Getting High Minded about Love and Haight
samples.title: Sometimes We Live No Particular Way but Our Own
samples.relation: Matthew Turner argues that a 'Playin' in the Band' jam — the band drifting from the tune into long collective improvisation and back — models a Stoic solution to free will shared by Epictetus, Spinoza, and Chuang Tzu: freedom is not uncaused choosing but responding well within constraints, so by the dichotomy of control there is no point resenting the band when it flubs a climax. Spinoza's definition of the free thing as one determined by its own nature, and Chuang Tzu's butcher who cuts oxen by spirit beyond skill, show the band letting the music 'play them' — Jerry's 'Tennessee Jed' riff never played the same way twice — as learned skill becomes second nature. Because the Dead jam within banks (keys, mutual listening, ability) yet generate something genuinely new and transcended every genre of 1960s music where the Monkees merely copied the Beatles, the Stoic attitude proves creative rather than quietist, an analogue for living freely within our own constraints.

samples.book: 093 - More Doctor Who and Philosophy - Regeneration Time
samples.title: 7. What the Doctor Can and Can’t Change
samples.relation: Delamont codifies the Whoniverse's four rules of time travel—time can be rewritten, fixed points cannot, knowing your future fixes it, and crossing your own timeline should be avoided—from cases like 'The Waters of Mars' (Adelaide's suicide restoring the fixed outcome), 'The Angels Take Manhattan' (Rory vanishing at the sight of his gravestone), 'Father's Day,' and 'The Girl Who Waited.' She then asks whether the Doctor could have avoided Trenzalore and argues the universe is hard-deterministic once amended with the laws of time travel, since rules 2–4 constrain action the way soft determinism's freedom from external forces would not allow. Tracing the causal dominoes back from the truth-field question through the Silence, River's creation, the Pandorica, and the Time Lords' pocket-universe broadcast to the crack in Amy's wall, she concludes he could not have avoided Trenzalore short of unwriting his entire history—'you can't change history if you're part of it.'

samples.book: 182 - Mad Men and Philosophy - Nothing Is as It Seems
samples.title: Bringing Corporations and Government Together
samples.relation: Guilfoy stages Galbraith's The Affluent Society against Friedman's Capitalism and Freedom through the Heineken case: Don's end-aisle display made Betty serve the beer at her dinner party, and when she found out she had been the target demographic she accused him ('You embarrassed me'). Galbraith's deep-self compatibilism holds that advertising-created desires are not genuinely ours, so Betty's choice was unfree, and that consumerism produces private wealth amid public squalor (the Cadillac picnic litter scene, the Madison Square Garden account Lane kills for lack of profit); Friedman's libertarian free will answers that Betty simply chose, desires are reasons rather than causes, and Pete's Admiral Negro-market pitch shows the market punishing racist irrationality. Both economists converge on the danger dramatized in 'The Inheritance': when Sterling Cooper sells corporations to congressmen and congressmen to corporations, consumers lose under either theory.

samples.book: 043 - The Golden Compass and Philosophy - God Bites the Dust
samples.title: The Golden Compass and Philosophy
samples.relation: Michaud asks whether a prophesied savior can be a hero: since Lyra can succeed only in ignorance of the witches' prophecy (Dr. Lanselius's condition), either others keep her ignorant and she saves the world or someone tells her and she fails, so the outcome never depends on her any more than Iorek's eating of Iofur's heart depends on bear choice. Frankfurt's counterexample, recast with the Magisterium's Fra Pavel standing by to force your choice, shows one can be blameworthy despite being unable to do otherwise, and Fischer's guidance control, a reasons-responsive decision-making mechanism that is your own, checked across possible worlds, explains why responsibility survives absent alternatives. But Lyra's case exposes a flaw in that account: her success hinges on things she cannot control, so responsibility is shared among all who kept the prophecy secret, and heroism lies in character and self-sacrifice rather than sole control of the outcome.

samples.book: 079 - Frankenstein and Philosophy - The Shocking Truth
samples.title: Frankenstein and Philosophy
samples.relation: Zuk argues Shelley needs the monster to be a free, responsible villain for her Romantic allegory against Enlightenment science to work, then puts him on trial: libertarian free will collides with Honderich's determinism, compatibilism demands only rational responsiveness to reasons, and Strawson's regress - built on Kant's opening demand that we make ourselves morally good or evil by free choice - suggests no one is ultimately responsible for character. The monster's biography tells against guilt: benevolent toward the De Laceys, beaten by Felix, shot after saving a drowning girl, then vowing 'eternal hatred and vengeance to all mankind' - a good nature corrupted beyond his control, overpowered by passion rather than acting with a clear head. Even Victor's dying encouragement to Walton's crew ('be men, or be more than men') concedes the creation was good in itself, so the novel indicts not science but its unguided release among the prejudiced.

samples.book: 032 - Bruce Springsteen and Philosophy - Darkness on the Edge of Truth
samples.title: Unity Born from Diversity
samples.relation: Shook narrates the 1984 Born in the U.S.A. tour — George Will's 'Yankee Doodle Springsteen' column, Reagan's Hammonton speech, Springsteen's refusal to be either campaign's tool — and reads the song as the hopeless story of a Vietnam-generation man's living death (the refinery that won't hire him, the dead brother and the Saigon woman) mistaken by flag-waving crowds for a patriotic anthem. He then maps the song's possible meanings onto democracy's possible destinies: Carl Schmitt's friend–enemy politics of national homogeneity and permanent emergency, Schlesinger's assimilationist Disuniting of America, and liberal cosmopolitanism's citizens of the world. Dewey's The Public and Its Problems wins: democracy must intelligently manage rather than eliminate diversity, each citizen holding a double loyalty to subgroup and to the democratic 'great community,' so being born in the U.S.A. is a responsibility and pride is properly placed in democratic ideals.

samples.book: 159 - The Expanse and Philosophy - So Far Out Into the Darkness
samples.title: Against Love of Nation
samples.relation: Applies George Orwell's distinction between patriotism (defensive devotion open to critique) and nationalism (obsessive, unstable, indifferent to reality) to Belt politics, reading Drummer as the patriot — she works for the Earther Fred Johnson, turns her guns on Belter radicals in 'Pyre', and refuses to whitewash Marco's massacres ('We're scavengers') — and Marco Inaros as the nationalist, whose asteroid genocide, treatment of Naomi as a welwala, and brainwashing of Filip ('All I did, I did for all Belters') display obsession, loyalty-transfer, and indifference to reality. The chapter's twist is that by Season 5 the patriots lose, because nationalists can always outbid defenders who play only defense, so neither Drummer nor Marco has the right attitude; Avasarala's finale call to 'turn every Belter, Martian, and Earther into this [the Rocinante crew]' makes cosmopolitanism — shared humanity over national loyalty — the show's real answer.

samples.book: 188 - The Ultimate South Park and Philosophy - Respect My Philosophah!
samples.title: THE ULTIMATE SOUTH PARK AND PHILOSOPHY
samples.relation: Kirby reads the 'Imaginationland' trilogy as a satire of post-9/11 America interpreted through Ulrich Beck's world risk society: the Pentagon generals, still thinking in Cold War categories like 'Project X' and Chinese imagination portals, embody Beck's denial response and end up voting to nuke Imaginationland, while Cartman's Rambo-style self-interest embodies the apathetic response. Socrates' practice of demanding definitions frames the chapter's question of what terrorism actually is (via Hoffman's five criteria), and Socratic ignorance about what one does not know is contrasted with the worse condition of not being able to know what you do not know. Kyle's courtroom speech that imaginary beings like Luke Skywalker and Santa are 'realer' than most real people, and Butters' creative power to imagine Santa back to life, point to Beck's cosmopolitan 'transformation': imagination and cross-border cooperation as the way out of risk panic.

samples.book: 039 - Jimmy Buffett and Philosophy - The Porpoise Driven Life
samples.title: “When the Coast is Clear”
samples.relation: Celia Bardwell-Jones asks how Parrothead tourism can be ethical when mass-market tourism walls the Caribbean inside an 'environmental bubble' of consumption — the 'ugly, stupid' tourist of Jamaica Kincaid's Antigua who never encounters the toured other as a fellow agent. Kant's Perpetual Peace sets the standard of hospitality, the stranger's right not to be treated as an enemy, and the chapter asks what duties fall on the traveler in return when tourist industries pressure host cultures 'not to be so damn foreign.' Buffett's novel A Salty Piece of Land supplies the alternative: Tully Mars is saved from free-floating survival when he drops anchor in the relationship with Cleopatra Highbourne — the 'song of the ocean' meeting 'a salty piece of land' — so that escape is redeemed by home, boundary-crossing, and self-reflection with culturally different others.

samples.book: 149 - Black Panther and Philosophy - What Can Wakanda Offer the World_
samples.title: 7 Should Wakanda Take Over the World The Ethics of International Power
samples.relation: Littmann asks whether Wakanda should take over the world, staging N'Jobu's and Killmonger's 'Wakanda could rule them all... the right way' plan against the history of benevolently justified empire: Roman civilization of barbarians, Kipling's white man's burden, and Mill's trusteeship argument for educating non-Europeans toward democracy. Plato's Republic case for rule by the wisest initially favors Wakandan conquest, but Kant's Perpetual Peace condemnation of conquering 'European savages,' Mill's own four reasons imperial rule goes wrong (ignorance of local conditions, lack of sympathy, partiality, exploitation), and Diderot's claim that distance from home erodes moral restraint convince him domination breeds abuse; he endorses Nakia's aid-and-refuge outreach and Mill's hope that the 'aristocracy of nationality' will one day look as wrong as racism.

samples.book: 174 - Indiana Jones and Philosophy - Why Did It Have to Be Socrates_
samples.title: 19 Meddling with (Almost) Incomprehensible Powers
samples.relation: Argues that archaeology can never escape politics: Nazi relic plunder for the planned Führermuseum, French removals at Angkor Wat, the UNESCO 1970 convention, and Zahi Hawass's cultural nationalism versus James Cuno's 'encyclopedic museums' all determine what Indy — or any archaeologist — may legitimately do. Measured against Alison Wylie's stewardship principle, Indy emerges as a 'loot-and-scoot' adventurer whose 'it belongs in a museum' cosmopolitanism sits uneasily with national patrimony claims, and the chapter weighs backward-looking title-based versus forward-looking value-based approaches to the Golden Idol, the Sankara Stone he returns, and the Cross of Coronado. It closes by asking whether the living can wrong the dead and vanished cultures, and whether the government 'top men' warehousing the Ark were right after all.

samples.book: 212 - The Olympics and Philosophy
samples.title: The Olympics and Philosophy
samples.relation: Milan Hosta traces a dialectical line from the individual athlete through nationalism and internationalism to the transnational Olympic movement, arguing individualism 'turns into itself again' since the whole order is reproduced by individuals like Paavo Nurmi ('I run for myself, not for Finland'). He reads Coubertin's 'sincere internationalism' as a moral epistemology of knowing others (glossed via Morgan and a Hegelian account of tolerance as recognizing but not truly accepting difference) against the hollow cosmopolitanism of tourism and 'popular ethnography.' Drawing on postmodern pluralism and the end of grand narratives, plus Hardt and Negri's Empire, he frames the IOC as a peace-preaching yet blood-bathed transnational power sustained by record-seeking individuals.

samples.book: 115 - Iron Man vs. Captain America and Philosophy - Give Me Liberty or Keep Me Safe
samples.title: 7. How Captain America and Iron Man Embody America
samples.relation: Altmann contrasts Tony's individualist cosmopolitanism - privatizing world peace, building Ultron alone - with Steve's community-rooted patriotism, the team player from war bonds through the Howling Commandos to Winter Soldier. Using Scruton's definition of patriotism as standing or falling together, MacIntyre's claim that morality grows only within a particular community, and Nussbaum's suggestion to be a patriot first and grow into a cosmopolitan, he concludes Cap's thoughtful patriotism is morally preferable while Tony's globe-saving individualism keeps backfiring. The best American would combine Tony's concern for the whole Earth with Steve's love of neighbor, so no civil war is needed.

samples.book: 173 - Inception and Philosophy - Because It's Never Just a Dream
samples.title: The Kick—Back to ‘Reality’
samples.relation: Richardson and McWilliams read Inception as an 'existential heist film' by diving through four layers of meaning. At the layer of reality they use Descartes's dream skepticism and wax argument, Hume on belief as custom and cause-effect, and Goffman on being shocked between frames to argue the film makes touch — the fall that wakes, pain ('pain is in the mind'), Saito's wrong-textured polyester carpet, the broken totems (Cobb's top, Arthur's loaded die, Ariadne's holed chess piece) — the only semi-trustworthy sense, while Mal, who locks her totem in the dollhouse safe and picks the dream, replays the cave prisoner who chooses the shadows. The car-chase layer ('downwards is the only way forwards'), Saito's 'old man filled with regrets' limbo, and the pharmacy dreamers who 'come to be woken up' are read through existentialism (Beckett's Waiting for Godot, Jaspers on loneliness and nothingness) and Peirce on the continuity of consciousness, with Cobb cast as the ideological existentialist who chooses action and reality where Cypher in The Matrix and Vanilla Sky's David face the same choice. The chapter then treats the film's reflexivity — the team as screenwriter/producer/director, the Escher-esque Penrose stairs, cross-cut dream time à la Peckinpah — as a lesson in film theory, and finally reaches phenomenology: Cobb's angry projection of Mal shows the dream world displaying his subjective meanings, against Arthur's calm, orderly hotel mindscape.

samples.book: 025 - The Beatles and Philosophy - Nothing You Can Think that Can't Be Thunk
samples.title: CHAPTER 2 “A CREATIVE TENSION”
samples.relation: The chapter traces the Beatles' rise as a case study in how novelty enters culture: Lennon and McCartney polarize into transgressive truth and melodic beauty, their 'creative tension' producing an emergent whole greater than either (the 'holding a mirror' songwriting method, their fused harmonies, the Decca audition versus Hamburg swings between commerce and authenticity). Hamburg is the underworld initiation where 'Mach Schau!' humiliation, absurdist humor read as Freudian catharsis, and Preludin-fueled marathon sets broke them out of English propriety into ecstatic physicality, before Epstein's suits and George Martin's harsh Abbey Road critique dragged the pendulum back toward rational professionalism. Against the Cartesian thesis that humanity is defined by the thinking mind ('I think, therefore I am'), the chapter reads 'Please Please Me,' Beatlemania's screaming crowds (citing Ehrenreich on female assertiveness and solidarity), and Rubber Soul as successive dialectical phase transitions integrating affect with intellect — a rock-and-roll answer to rationalized modernity, in James's wave-crest image of novelty flung ahead of history.

samples.book: 047 - Anime and Philosophy - Wide Eyed Wonder
samples.title: Is Everybody Disembodied (or, Have We Always Been Posthuman Beings )
samples.relation: Stevens uses the film's closing voice-over 'I am Tetsuo' in Otomo's Akira to run the classic identity-and-mind problems: Heraclitus's river and Plutarch's Ship of Theseus ask whether the grotesquely transformed, Akira-absorbed Tetsuo is still the same person, while Descartes's cogito — riffed as 'cogito ergo Tetsuo' — Turing's Test, and Searle's Chinese Room test whether a voice that seems to think proves a thinker behind it (syntax is not yet shown sufficient for semantics, though Edwin Hutchins's distributed cognition reads the Room from the inside out). Weighing embodiment (Pinker's brain-makes-mind, Dennett's self as a 'center of narrative gravity') against disembodiment (Akira levelling Neo-Tokyo from nothing but cryogenically stored remains; Tetsuo's matter teleportation), he concludes through the problem of representation — every utterance is re-presented, as in Augustine's guilty tears over Dido — that we always treat semblances of thinkers as thinkers, so we may have always been decentered, re-presented, posthuman beings no different from Tetsuo and Akira.

samples.book: 061 - Sherlock Holmes and Philosophy - The Footprints of a Gigantic Mind
samples.title: The Evil Genius that Turns Moriarty into a Brain in a Vat
samples.relation: Samardzija reads Star Trek's holodeck Moriarty as Descartes updated: Data plays Holmes on the holodeck while Dr. Pulaski's Nietzschean jibe (from 'The Illogical Necessary' in Human, All Too Human) denies that computation can be human, and the holographic Moriarty proves his sentience not by deduction but by feelingCrowded intuitions first and then invoking Descartes' cogito ergo sum to Picard. In 'Ship in a Bottle' he nests a simulation of the Enterprise inside the Holmes holodeck to trick the crew into believing he has escaped — an evil-genius, brain-in-a-vat scenario that ends with Picard admitting our own reality 'might be nothing more than an elaborate simulation.' The paradox is that only the unemotional android Data can detect the deception, so rationality bars him from humanity while Moriarty stays eternally deceived into thinking he has become human — and Doyle's own 'hereditary tendencies' account of Moriarty's evil, the chapter notes, is a Victorian biological determinism the hologram rebels against.

samples.book: 091 - It's Always Sunny and Philosophy - The Gang Gets Analyzed
samples.title: It’s Always Sunny and Philosophy
samples.relation: Roger Hunt answers 'what do philosophers do?' through Dennis's seduction methodology. Frank embodies empiricism, leaving the comfort of principle for the messiness of the world as Hume did when he found no impression of causation, space, or time; Mac embodies rationalism, reasoning with total confidence from a principle he cannot doubt, as Descartes did from the cogito; and the dialectic of Socrates and Plato, questioning beliefs in dialogue to see what survives scrutiny, describes philosophy as it is actually practiced. Boethius's Consolation - the imprisoned author consoled by dialogues with Lady Philosophy - supplies the frame of philosophy as an encounter with a woman one pursues, and each D.E.N.N.I.S. step maps onto the craft: Demonstrating value to the problem, Engaging physically in its awkward grind, Nurturing dependence through thesis panic, Neglect and Inspiring hope on the road to the defense, then Separating entirely - 'be a sociopath about it.'

samples.book: 168 - Heroes and Philosophy - Buy the Book, Save the World
samples.title: NOTES
samples.relation: Distinguishes Matt Parkman's supernatural telepathy from the 'mundane mind reading' everyone performs, then argues even Matt's power cannot solve the problem of other minds: the suicidal woman's thoughts he hears in the bar ('One Giant Leap') could be part of a Maury-Parkman-style illusion, and a brain-to-brain link could never rule out that others are Chalmers-style philosophical zombies. After grounding the skepticism in Descartes' cogito and method of doubt, it defends our everyday attribution of minds by analogy (Audrey Hanson reading Claire's insincerity) on pragmatic grounds, and maps Matt's progression from hearing thoughts to nightmare manipulation and compulsion onto the four adaptive functions philosophers assign to mind reading: interpretation, prediction, coordination, and influence. It closes by showing why neuroimaging-based technological mind reading remains a pipe dream, since brain recordings are quantitative syntax without semantics.

samples.book: 093 - More Doctor Who and Philosophy - Regeneration Time
samples.title: 9. How the Doctor Knows
samples.relation: Smithka argues the Doctor is a reliabilist about knowledge rather than a Cartesian strong foundationalist: using 'Amy's Choice,' 'The Beast Below' (the glass of water, the engine room, Amy's inference that the Star Whale came willingly), 'Silence in the Library' (the chicken-leg experiment implicating the Vashta Nerada), and Davros's Dalek trials in 'Genesis of the Daleks,' she shows him trusting perception in the right causal chain and reasoning inductively and abductively—Peirce's inference to the best explanation—instead of demanding Cartesian certainty. Against Descartes's dream and evil-genius skepticism, updated as Putnam-style brain-in-a-vat scenarios via the Dream Crabs of 'Last Christmas' and the Dream Lord's two-worlds game, she deploys Goldman's three criteria for perceptual knowledge: justification is packed into reliable belief-forming processes, and doubt is warranted only in known abnormal contexts like funhouses or Dream Lord games.

samples.book: 062 - Inception and Philosophy - Ideas to Die For
samples.title: The Kick—Back to ‘Reality’
samples.relation: The authors read the film in descending layers: reality as an ideology of touch and unreliable sensory experience, framed by Descartes's wax thought experiment and dream argument, with the kick explained through Hume's account of belief as custom and the totems as broken game pieces marking broken people (Mal's choice of the dream echoing prisoners returning to Plato's cave). The heist is then read as an existentialist drama where Cobb's 'downwards is the only way forwards' rejects the passive waiting of Beckett's Waiting for Godot and the pharmacy dreamers, with Jaspers's analysis of solitude making Limbo a hell of lonely regret that only an encounter with another can end. The chapter then argues the film is reflexively about movies (the crew mirrors a film crew, the Penrose stairs expose cinema's flat illusions, crosscutting manufactures time) before ending on Descartes's unresolved doubt about whether the final reality deserves our trust.

samples.book: 160 - Fallout and Philosophy - Thinking Outside the Shelter
samples.title: Notes
samples.relation: The Funkes apply Clark and Chalmers's extended mind hypothesis to the Pip-Boy, arguing it meets all three criteria for cognitive extension - availability (worn at all times), reliability (trusted rad and health monitoring), and active cognitive engagement (V.A.T.S. offloads targeting calculations) - so it is part of the Sole Survivor's and Courier's minds, as in 'The Glowing Sea' and the search for Virgil's cure. Donna Haraway's cyborg frames this human-machine hybridity alongside cyberdogs and Kellogg, but Fallout inverts her liberationist vision: the Pip-Boy is a survival lifeline forced by the wasteland, not an emancipatory choice, making the cyborg a dystopian necessity. Comparing the Pip-Boy with cochlear implants, prosthetics, and brain-computer interfaces, and the Old World Blues Think Tank with a dehumanizing bio-tech extreme, the chapter uses Alison Kafer's feminist crip critique to insist real augmentation carries pain, stigma, and unequal access the game's frictionless fiction erases, closing on a cautious transhumanist note.

samples.book: 047 - Anime and Philosophy - Wide Eyed Wonder
samples.title: The Transforming Body
samples.relation: McBlane reads Oshii's Ghost in the Shell as staging the collision between a humanist framework — Cartesian ghost-in-shell dualism where consciousness is the seat of identity — and a posthuman 'mindbody' of distributed cognition in which the body is an informational circuit extending into the net, so a data body is still a body. Motoko's crisis (is the real me the organic brain, the ghost, or nothing?) deepens through the hacked garbage-truck man ('There's nothing sadder than a puppet without a ghost') and resolves only in her fusion with the Puppet Master, whose line 'Your effort to remain what you are is what limits you' enacts the shift from one ghost to multiple, distributed subjectivities ending in a little girl's body with 'The net is vast.' Heidegger's Dasein and being-in-the-world supply the claim that access to Being expands beyond the human into technological and informational modes, while the film's angelic transcendence imagery shows how residual humanist mind-body splits persist even in a posthuman story.

samples.book: 115 - Iron Man vs. Captain America and Philosophy - Give Me Liberty or Keep Me Safe
samples.title: 21. The Extended Fight
samples.relation: Porot applies Clark and Chalmers's extended mind to the final Civil War fight: Iron Man extends his cognition technologically (Friday analyzing Cap's fight pattern mid-bout, JARVIS remembering to suggest calling Pepper), while Captain America extends his mind socially through trusted, autonomous teammates - 'Alright, Sam, what's the plan?' - and that social extension is precisely what wins when Bucky autonomously steps in. Bostrom's single-purpose AI (the stapler maximizer) explains Ultron as what happens when the technological extension is made autonomous and limitless, which is why Stark's suit extensions must remain vetted, worthy instruments he takes full responsibility for ('That was me'). The two kinds of extension then explain the Bucky dispute - Cap's 'you had no choice' versus Stark's 'he still did it' - which the author reframes away from the free-will-versus-determinism framing toward Black Panther's point that Bucky is a victim whose agency Hydra stole.

samples.book: 243 - The Philosophy of Christopher Nolan
samples.title: We Are the Change That We Seek
samples.relation: These essays treat time, selfhood and substance across Nolan's films. Fosl argues Nolan's selves (Leonard, Bill in Following, the Borden twins, Bruce Wayne) are unstable narratives signified through manipulable objects, invoking Locke on memory-based identity, Augustine on memoria, Nietzsche on forgetting and Sartre/Gadamer on the manipulable past. LaRocca applies Clark and Chalmers's Extended Mind Thesis to Memento, arguing Leonard's tattoos and Polaroids are literal external memories whose deliberate falsification ('Don't believe his lies') makes him morally culpable for murder. Willis uses Lacan's gaze and objet a to read Following's voyeur-becomes-viewed structure and 'the box' as a lure. McGowan reads Interstellar through Hegel: the mysterious 'they' who opened the wormhole are revealed as future humanity, dissolving substance into subject and licensing Cooper's retroactive causality as the 'ghost' who saves Murph.

samples.book: 157 - Dungeons and Dragons and Philosophy - Read and Gain Advantage on All Wisdom Checks
samples.title: Dungeons and Dragons and Philosophy
samples.relation: Levi Bryant uses the D&D universe to expound a 'flat ontology' of active substances: every entity, from enchanted swords to white dragons, has a virtual proper being (powers or 'affects') that actualizes variable 'local manifestations' depending on circumstances like lighting or armor. Adopting Andy Clark and David Chalmers's extended mind hypothesis, he argues a blind man with a cane, a smartphone owner, or Elric wielding Stormbringer is a literally different mind or entity, and that alliances (Raistlin's Staff of Magius, a warrior's plate armor) generate genuinely new powers rather than mere tool-use. Against Democritus's atomism, he holds aggregates can be individuals, and the game's dice embody his claim that chance produces necessity: throws generate 'regimes of attraction' no DM or player controls. D&D thus mirrors our own world of hidden powers, aleatory encounters and collectives of humans and nonhumans.

samples.book: 034 - iPod and Philosophy - iCon of an ePoch
samples.title: After Forgetting
samples.relation: Sturgis argues that iPods plus the collaborative Web 2.0 will end education's age of memorization: the school 'cheaters' storing test answers in lyrics files are early adopters of a world where, as Plato's Meno already allowed, knowledge can be retrieved rather than remembered, and a remote server is no more crash-prone than a brain ('the server could crash, but so could I'). His own podcasted environmental-ethics course shows Socratic, question-driven lecturing and radio's 'theater of the mind' reaching distance learners, while MIT OpenCourseWare and Berkeley webcasts (a trucker listening to Hubert Dreyfus) globalize elite content. Following Dewey on reflection and artistry, he predicts a post-factual pedagogy of assessing sources -- he catches Wikipedia misreading an iPod '90 percent market share' claim -- collaborative creation, and candid acceptance that we are already integrated with technological devices.

samples.book: 196 - Terminator and Philosophy - I'll Be Back, Therefore I Am
samples.title: NOTES
samples.relation: Butler argues the films' humans-versus-machines picture rests on a false dichotomy: we are ourselves 'meat machines,' and functionalism makes minds computational processes realizable in silicon as much as neurons - illustrated by a Henrietta thought experiment (adapted from William Lycan) in which a friend gradually replaced with T-101 parts remains the same conscious person, and refusing this is 'human chauvinism.' Following Dawkins's extended phenotype and Andy Clark's natural-born cyborgs, he claims our tools are components of our minds, so Skynet and even the Terminator films themselves (making Cameron a cyborg of his cameras and editing suites) are extensions of human nature rather than alien 'Others.' Judgment Day, if it came, would be human suicide rather than genocide, so the real question is what values we build into our technology - 'no fate but what we make for ourselves.'

samples.book: 074 - Planet of the Apes and Philosophy - Great Apes Think Alike
samples.title: Planet of the Apes and Philosophy
samples.relation: Kristin Andrews uses Taylor's silent attempts to show Zira he has a mind - mouthing answers, wiggling his fingers when she mentions the Hopkins Manual Dexterity Test - to stage the problem of other minds, pushing against Descartes's claim that language is required for thought and Mill's argument from analogy, while Dr. Zaius can always redescribe it all as 'a definite gift for mimicry.'
