Drawing on her fieldwork with the orangutan Cecep (the leaf-wiping pantomime, guiding the frightened Aldrin home from the turtle scare), she argues against reducing mindreading to false-belief tasks and for knowing minds through shared interaction, inductive overhypotheses, and natural context. She ends with an extended-mind point - 'when you're in a cage, you act caged,' and we offload thinking onto our homes and tools - so lab studies can show what apes can do but never what they can't.

samples.book: 031 - Johnny Cash and Philosophy - The Burning Ring of Truth
samples.title: The Doors Are Never Locked
samples.relation: Held reads Cash's Walk the Line retort "Well, they're not Christians then" as a thesis about redemption: since, with Augustine, we rejoice most at the sinner saved, and since the Sermon on the Mount forbids judging what we cannot know (anyone's deep character), humility demands withholding condemnation and hoping even the worst can change. He contrasts Christian redemption, a revaluation of the person that needs outside grace (Cash needed June and the Carters; nobody is self-made), with Nietzsche's attack on redemption as slave-morality self-hatred, granting that Nietzsche's eternal recurrence also revalues the past but objecting that self-revaluation collapses into rationalization, as Cash's Saul in Man in White shows. Forgiveness proper requires repentance and a solvent character, like paying off a debt; the shame of the "Long Black Veil" woman shows why; and because we see "through a glass darkly," nobody, not the Reno murderer, not Joe Bean, is beyond hope, which is why the doors are never locked and why execution or life without parole claims a judgment of moral worth that is not ours to make.

samples.book: 209 - Basketball and Philosophy - Thinking Outside the Paint
samples.title: Hoosiers and the Meaning of Life
samples.relation: Michael Peterson argues that Hoosiers is a microcosm of life's meaning: Aristotle's eudaimonia frames the characters' searches (Norman Dale rebuilding his career, Shooter his self-esteem and his bond with son Everett), and Dale's 'in my book, we're going to be winners' speech shows that character, unselfish teamwork, and playing to potential - virtue learned by doing, as coaching models moral instruction - matter more than the scoreboard against South Bend Central. The film's second chances (Principal Summers's clean slate, Whit's return, Dale's hiring of the town drunk Shooter) reveal that character alone is insufficient: mercy and forgiveness, which Hannah Arendt traces to Jesus, reframe an unchangeable past and open a future. Peterson then surveys worldviews - naturalism (Bertrand Russell's 'accidental collocations of atoms'), postmodernism (Derrida's deconstruction), Hinduism's Atman-Brahman - and argues only Christian theism, in which God's nature is love (Aquinas), can ground the character and forgiveness the film dramatizes.

samples.book: 104 - Red Rising and Philosophy - Break the Chains!
samples.title: 15. Death Begets Death
samples.relation: The Bocks trace Darrow's education out of vengeance: in Plato's tripartite soul the spirited part (anger) must obey reason, and Aristotle's virtue of mildness—anger at the right things, toward the right people, for the right length of time—is the golden mean between slavish and irascible that Darrow has not yet reached. Darrow learns the difference when he hands Titus over to Cassius's vendetta and admits 'That wasn't justice': retribution in Kant's lex talionis tradition must be dispassionate and proportional, while vengeance is past-oriented and insatiable, and Darrow's own bombing of the Ganymede docks shows how troubling even his 'justice' remains. Against Darrow's violent justice-in-love the chapter sets Martin Luther King Jr.'s agape and loving-forgiveness—Sevro hanging and then forgiving Cassius, Darrow forgiving Tactus, Mustang pulling her brother's legs for a merciful death—closing with King's warning that constructive ends can never justify destructive means, and Darrow's own admission that 'the war is not over.'

samples.book: 141 - Avatar_ The Last Airbender and Philosophy - Wisdom from Aang to Zuko
samples.title: Opening Up Possibilities
samples.relation: Argues, through Hilde Lindemann's relational account of personhood, that Zuko genuinely is all of the identities others hold him in (disappointing son, villain, ally) because being a person is a social practice of expression, recognition, and response. Aang's decision to hear Zuko out at the Western Air Temple, Iroh's stubborn refusal to accept Ozai's script for him (his anger itself recognizing Zuko as an agent capable of choosing otherwise), and Katara's historically-sensitive slow trust open up the possible future in which Zuko can become trustworthy, while the Earth Kingdom villagers' rejection of him in 'Zuko Alone' shows how weight of history and stereotype can shut possibility down. The chapter insists this is not letting wrongdoers off the hook: genuine apology, repair, and moral anger remain required (contrasting the Brock Turner case), but only a moral community that holds people in personhood makes redemption possible, so society should be arranged to give everyone the Iros and Aangs that Zuko was lucky to have.

samples.book: 010 - Mel Gibson's Passion and Philosophy - The Cross, the Questions, the Controversy
samples.title: Mel Gibson’s Passion and Philosophy
samples.relation: Walls argues the controversy lies not in the gore but in who died on the cross and why, and shows Gibson weaving the three classic atonement theories: Christ crushing the serpent in Gethsemane as the Christus-Victor ransom (with Augustine's mousetrap image), the Isaiah 53 scourging and Gibson's own hand driving the nail as Anselm-style penal substitution in which the innocent dies so the guilty Barabbas in each of us goes free, and the transformed characters (Mary Magdalene, Simon of Cyrene, the good thief, the kneeling soldier) as Abelard's moral influence. Against Kant's charge that atonement is a superstitious substitute for moral transformation, he cites Swinburne and Quinn: pleading the atonement requires repentance, and the tens of thousands of reported conversions and confessions show it transforms lives. He concludes that any adequate account needs all three theories, objective payment and subjective transformation alike, and that atonement aims at mercy and reconciliation rather than retribution.

samples.book: 066 - Neil Gaiman and Philosophy - Gods Gone Wild!
samples.title: Neil Gaiman and Philosophy
samples.relation: Najwa Al-Tabaa reads Sandman: Season of Mists through Derrida's paradox that only the unforgivable can truly be forgiven: Morpheus's freeing of Nada works as forgiveness precisely because condemning his lover to Hell was unforgivable, while Lucifer, who was never wronged by the damned, can give them only a devalued semblance of pardon, and they cling to punishment they feel they deserve. She then brings in Foucault's Discipline and Punish and Bentham's Panopticon to read the angels' rebuilt Hell of redemption as the modern rehabilitative prison, where watched souls are expected to reform themselves. The experiment fails, she argues, because redemption is imposed without hearing the prisoners, violating Derrida's condition that forgiveness needs a shared language, so the inmates prefer Lucifer's honest eternity of despair to a salvation they never asked for, a lesson about real prisons that seek rehabilitation through punishment.

samples.book: 115 - Iron Man vs. Captain America and Philosophy - Give Me Liberty or Keep Me Safe
samples.title: 16. Would You Buy a Used Car from This Avenger
samples.relation: Ericson uses the used-car litmus test to examine trust in the MCU: through McLeod's three criteria and Peperzak's contrast of the objectifying and interactive approaches, Tony's control-seeking distance (the lone-gun-slinger act of Iron Man 2) fails trust while Steve's soldier-style trust anchors the Winter Soldier thriller against Fury's 'This isn't freedom, this is fear' and HYDRA's coercion-eliminating project. Plato's rule that power should go only to those who do not want it explains why Cap can be entrusted with superpowers, Nietzsche's megalomaniac late letters frame Tony's drive to 'cleave history in two' by building Ultron and then the messianic Vision, and Banner's Hulk illustrates the Freudian road from repression to sublimation as the condition of self-trust. It ends with Cap's concealment of Bucky's killing of Tony's parents as the betrayal of trust that only a decision to forgive might repair.

samples.book: 048 - The Red Sox and Philosophy - Green Monster Meditations
samples.title: Forgiveness and the Fenway Faithful
samples.relation: Rory Kraft uses Aristotle's virtue ethics to explain why Red Sox Nation forgave Tim Wakefield (whose mistake Aaron Boone turned into the 2003 ALCS-ending homer) and Ted Williams, but scapegoated Bill Buckner for 'the error' and eventually cast off Manny Ramirez. Because Aristotle judges a complete life, one swallow does not make a summer, Buckner's .991 fielding percentage and 2,715 hits should contextualize his lapse, yet some acts are bad without degrees like Aristotle's adultery, theft and murder, and a World Series-deciding error crossed that line. Kraft distinguishes Aristotle's categories, Wakefield's mistake (ignorance of Boone's changed plan) versus Buckner's misadventure (contrary to reasonable expectation) versus Manny's voluntary injustices, concluding that learning when to forgive players who are family taught the Nation what forgiveness itself means, sealed by Buckner's 2008 standing ovation.

samples.book: 054 - The Onion and Philosophy - Fake News Story True, Alleges Indignant Area Professor
samples.title: Gene For Pedantry Same As Gene For Philosophy
samples.relation: Loader's chapter is a spread of fake 'Existential Times' news parodies: an uncompliant student who answers every robot thought experiment with 'But you're not' drives his professor to swearing over the problem of other minds; Wisconsin scientists find the self as a half-centimeter of Silly Putty in the neck, joking that Hume 'may simply have been looking in the wrong place' when introspection found only a bundle of perceptions; a poll finds not one American philosopher has read Hegel's Phenomenology of Spirit beyond 'the bit about the master and the slave'; and a student essay on Sartre's Existentialism and Humanism wanders off into Planet of the Apes and calls Sartre 'Mr Horse.' The Philososcope prescribes page 232 of Heidegger's Being and Time, a movie loser quotes Nietzsche ('There is always some madness in love') before falling into a pond, an archaeology department's found remains of God back Nietzsche's 'God is dead,' and a Marxist begs capitalism to hold off collapsing until her book is published—philosophy satirized as pedantry, posing, and self-importance.

samples.book: 073 - The Wire and Philosophy - This America, Man
samples.title: The Wire and Philosophy
samples.relation: Vannatta reads Season Four through Hegel's master-slave dialectic of recognition: Marlo's ultimatum to Bodie, Lex killing Fruit for Patrice, and D'Angelo's chess lesson (the pawn as slave producing for the king) all dramatize the struggle for recognition, while Marx's inversion of Hegel explains the alienation of the dockworkers, McNulty exiled to harbor patrol, and Freamon buried in pawn-shop detail by the chain of master-slave directives from Rawls through Marimow. The heart of the chapter is education: Prezbo's dice-and-card math projects embody Dewey's synthesis of child and curriculum against the 'banking concept' Freire attacked, but 'You don't teach math. You teach the test' shows the institutional logic winning, and Parenti's grant-funded project class with Colvin illustrates Freire's warning that the oppressor's humanitarian false generosity treats the corner kids as objects of study rather than partners in dialogue, leaving even its successes unable to show the kids why corner life is problematic.

samples.book: 122 - Westworld and Philosophy - Mind Equals Blown
samples.title: Humanization A Violent Phenomenon
samples.relation: Spanakos reads the hosts' season-one rebellion through Fanon's decolonization theory, itself a revision of Hegel's master-slave dialectic: as the settler 'brings the native into existence,' Ford and Delos create the hosts, assigning their identities and roles, while the master 'laughs at the consciousness of the slave' because the hosts' recognition is not freely given. Fanonian violence is ethical, justified, and transformative: Maeve's jailbreak and Dolores's execution of Ford (rather than her tormentor, the Man in Black, whom she sees as the system's victim) are acts that make the colonized a maker of history, while Bernard - who speaks his creator's language and has no culture or past of his own, like Fanon's assimilated African bourgeoisie - shows violence that does not liberate. The chapter closes that the park dehumanizes the masters too, so William's collapse into the Man in Black proves Fanon's point that the colonizer cannot free himself; humanization is a violent phenomenon.

samples.book: 010 - Mel Gibson's Passion and Philosophy - The Cross, the Questions, the Controversy
samples.title: Mel Gibson’s Passion and Philosophy
samples.relation: Lawler charges that Gibson's atonement theology, in which the more barbaric the torture the greater the redemption, imprisons Christianity at the stage of Hegel's 'Unhappy Consciousness', where an infinite God is sundered from abject sinful humanity and a priestly mediator is needed. Reading the film through the master-slave dialectic (impotent master Pilate versus the dignified slave Simon of Cyrene; the world of separate egos as Hobbes's war of all against all), he argues that what dies on the cross is the separate ego itself, and that what rises is Geist, the 'I' that is 'We' of the loving human community. Against Tertullian's credo quia absurdum, and using Pascal's 'heart has its reasons' alongside Hegel's dialectical reason, he reads 'you are gods' and the prodigal son as teaching every person's essential divinity, so the film's own art (the Mater Dolorosa, our identification with the flesh-and-blood Jesus) implicitly undermines the separatist theology Gibson intends.

samples.book: 035 - Star Trek and Philosophy - The Wrath of Kant
samples.title: “Its Continuing Mission”
samples.relation: Argues that Star Trek's real subject is Hegelian recognition: a society is worth living in when every member's claims count as reasons and their talents get developed. It reads 'The Measure of a Man' (Data winning legal personhood), 'The Outcast' (Riker defending the J'naii Soren), and DS9's 'Past Tense' Bell Riots as dramas of winning recognition, and maps the Romulan-Reman and Stratos-Troglyte hierarchies onto Hegel's master-slave dialectic, contrasting Descartes's solipsistic cogito with Hegel's claim that self-awareness needs another. Since recognition requires more than non-interference against Locke-style atomism, the Federation's appeal lies in positive liberties — education, open debate, guaranteed basic needs — even though the shows oddly skip elections and democratic politics, a tension the authors flag through Leonard Nimoy's praise of a world with 'no political agenda.'

samples.book: 044 - Led Zeppelin and Philosophy - All Will Be Revealed
samples.title: Led Zeppelin and Art
samples.relation: Shain uses Hegel's master-slave dialectic and the struggle for recognition to explain the band: Page and Jones formed Zeppelin because recognition as top session players wasn't enough, and the drive for critic and peer recognition — which varied by hierarchy, as when Bonham said 'If Buddy Rich says I'm shit, then I'm shit' — pushed the band from the bombastic early albums to the achievement of Led Zeppelin IV and Physical Graffiti. Recognition extends to groupies (association and gratification, sharpening feminism's empowerment-versus-objectification dilemma about Des Barres) and to the high-art question: claims like 'Stairway as landmark artistic achievement of the twentieth century' misfire, Shain argues, because using high-art elements such as improvisation or minimalism can simply make better pop culture without lifting Zeppelin into the art tradition.

samples.book: 008 - Woody Allen and Philosophy - You Mean My Whole Fallacy Is Wrong_
samples.title: And There Is No Escape
samples.relation: Abrams reads Allen through Foucault's panopticon: modern society is unlimited voyeurism in which the medieval God whose 'eyes are on us always' has been replaced by the omniscient gaze of Film — Cliff's exposé documentary forcing Lester to watch his own life in Crimes and Misdemeanors, Tom Baxter stepping off the screen in The Purple Rose of Cairo, and the nested eavesdropping layers of Another Woman, which he counts to infinity via Noël Carroll's 'mass art'. Against Mary Nichols's virtue-ethics reading, he argues Allen's ethics is Nietzschean self-fashioning: Judah lives 'beyond good and evil' where Raskolnikov failed, Allan Felix sheds the Bogart alter ego and 'gives style' to his character in Play It Again, Sam, while Eve in Interiors stages Hegel's master–slave dialectic, the 'master' artist dependent for her identity on those she objectifies.

samples.book: 012 - Star Wars and Philosophy - More Powerful than You Can Possibly Imagine
samples.title: An Empire of Fear and Trembling
samples.relation: Cameron reads the Emperor's dominion through Hegel's master-slave dialectic and struggle for recognition: fear is the Empire's currency, from Alderaan's destruction as visible demonstration ('fear will keep the local systems in line') to Vader's deliberately undefined threats ('The Emperor is not as forgiving as I am'), while hatred binds the Sith Master to Maul, Dooku, and Vader. Because the master can never win recognition from an unequal slave, Palpatine's will-to-power rule is a historical dead end, whereas the slave - Anakin laboring in Watto's shop, Luke overcoming his fear in the cave and under Yoda - can transform himself through work and courage. Vader's final turn is thus his achievement of a new self-consciousness, recognizing himself as 'something other than a slave' at the moment Luke's unshakeable faith forces the truth on him.

samples.book: 008 - Woody Allen and Philosophy - You Mean My Whole Fallacy Is Wrong_
samples.title: Humor and Philosophy
samples.relation: Ascione deploys Schopenhauer's theory of laughter — the sudden, paradoxical subsumption of an object under a heterogeneous concept — as the framework for showing how Annie Hall's gags do philosophical work. The subtitled balcony conversation exposes the self-monitoring deception of new romance, the street-interview 'love fades' scene smuggles in the unpopular thesis that lasting romantic love is mythical (culminating in the dead-shark line), the grammar-school reunion raises questions about what shapes adult character, and the 'dynamite ham' dinner, the pastrami-on-white-with-mayo, and the California scenes diagnose Alvy's own New York provincialism. Because humor suspends judgment and deflects resistance, Allen can deliver social and cultural analysis that audiences would reject if stated straight.

samples.book: 019 - Monty Python and Philosophy - Nudge Nudge, Think Think!
samples.title: Just Desserts
samples.relation: Asks how the exploding-glutton Mr. Creosote sequence in 'The Autumn Years' of The Meaning of Life can provoke laughter rather than horror, given that Creosote shares the monster's marks of physiological impossibility and disgusting category-violation (like Frankenstein's monster or the Alien). The answer: horror requires disgust plus fear, and Creosote, like the slapstick clown, is marked as neither able to harm nor be harmed, so the audience's fear-condition for horror is never met. A second layer of the laughter is vindictive: the maitre d''s wafer-thin mint is retributive justice, a morality-play punishment for gluttony in the lineage of Spenser's Gluttony and Dante's Inferno, so black comedy trades on our sense that the victim deserves what he gets.

samples.book: 096 - Hannibal Lecter and Philosophy - The Heart of the Matter
samples.title: 14. A Funny Thing Happened on the Way to the Dinner Party
samples.relation: Westfall sorts Lecter's humor into mockery ('I hope you're not too ugly'), expressions of power ('Are you setting a new standard of care?', delivered while hanging from a noose), and inside jokes ('I'm having an old friend for dinner', 'I wouldn't do that to the food, Tobias'), arguing against Noël Carroll that something can be frightening and funny at once because the joke is itself an exercise of power. He shows how the television series converts Harris's cruel mockery into displays of control, and how in-jokes addressed to the audience — Mikkelsen's census-taker callback to Hopkins's fava-beans line — pull viewers into complicity, a subtle fourth-wall break that is itself an expression of power.

samples.book: 120 - Amy Schumer and Philosophy - Brainwreck!
samples.title: 7. Amy Schumer or the Incongruities
samples.relation: Pits Freud's psychoanalytic theory of wit, where harmless nonsense smuggles tendentious sexual content past the superego's censor, against the incongruity theory of comic amusement, using 'Boner Doctor' as the test case. Carroll argues the psychoanalytic account makes the superego absurdly gullible, citing Foucault on how thoroughly sexuality is now discussed, and cannot capture what is specific to Schumer. Incongruity theory can: sketches like 'Sexting' and Trainwreck's doll analogy for infidelity generate laughter from violated norms of ladylike decorum, exposing her feminism as a sustained subversion of the modest, uninterested stereotype of womanhood.

samples.book: 030 - Pink Floyd and Philosophy - Careful with that Axiom, Eugene!
samples.title: To Join in with the Game
samples.relation: Gracyk argues Waters is wrong that Pink Floyd ended when he quit in 1985: Waters's case rests on an illicit use of the identity of indiscernibles, since if losing Waters's lyrics destroys the band's identity, then losing Barrett's or Wright's, or adding 'Lucifer Sam,' would too, which proves too much. Borrowing Locke's distinction between the same man and the same person (the oak that remains the same oak through change; the unrecognized Syd in Abbey Road's Studio Three) and Kant's contrast between free and dependent beauty to explain how intentions change aesthetic evaluation, he defends actual intentionalism over hypothetical intentionalism: Hendrix really sings 'kiss the sky,' and interviews with Waters genuinely aid interpretation of Wish You Were Here. He then argues for collective agency, that groups can have intentions through members charged to act responsibly on the group's behalf, so no single member can disband a collective: Waters had a duty to leave, Gilmour, Mason, and Wright were entitled to continue the group's longstanding intention of making and performing original music, and the Echoes compilation is therefore an accurate portrait of the real Pink Floyd.

samples.book: 160 - Fallout and Philosophy - Thinking Outside the Shelter
samples.title: Notes
samples.relation: Matthew Watts sorts Fallout's artificial beings into cyborgs, synths, and pure robots and tests each against a theory of the self: Locke's memory theory explains the Robobrain socialites of Vault 118 and Nick Valentine's implanted prewar past, Parfit's psychological continuity (identity as a matter of degree) makes the Old World Blues Think Tank a caricature of a self stretched too thin, and Putnam's machine-table functionalism with multiple realizability (the Red Menace holotape running on any hardware) undermines Covenant's SAFE test by making function, not substrate, the mark of a mind. DiMA's excision of his own guilty memory in Far Harbor shows identity as Evan Thompson's enactive process rather than stored recall, since pruning memories can maintain or improve the self-in-progress. For moral standing below full personhood, Nussbaum's capabilities approach fits Curie's flourishing (research, companionship, watching a sunset in a synth body) and Singer's sentience criterion fits Victor the Securitron's avoidance of harm, exposing 'substrate prejudice' as a robot analog of speciesism - down to ED-E's triumphant arrival on the West Coast.

samples.book: 148 - Black Mirror and Philosophy - Dark Reflections
samples.title: A Dilemma
samples.relation: The chapter asks 'Is your cookie you?', running theories of personal identity through Black Mirror's copies: the soul theory surfaces when Clayton signs away his 'digital self'; Locke's memory theory implies Cookie-Greta is Greta - a reductio, since one person cannot be wholly in two places at once (the same problem for Ashley Too and the thousand Hang the DJ simulations) - and the perdurantist patch recasts Greta and her cookie as time-slices of one four-dimensional person. Physical theories (Olson's animalism, Unger's brain-essentialism) rule out survival by upload, so Yorkie dies when her body dies even though digital Yorkie continues in San Junipero; Parfit's no-self bundle view and the teletransporter case then dissolve the fear, since there is no ego to lose and ordinary survival is 'about as bad' as being destroyed and replaced by a replica. The upshot: the punishment and immortality plots (Joe's million-year Christmas loop, San Junipero) require cookies to be both conscious and psychologically connected in the right way, and the episodes' horror depends on leaving that genuinely uncertain.

samples.book: 046 - Mr. Monk and Philosophy - The Curious Case of the Defective Detective
samples.title: Mr. Monk Is Mr. Monk
samples.relation: Malloy runs the classic theories of personal identity through Monk episodes. Bodily (really brain) identity fails when 'the Monk' — the reckless medicated alter of 'Mr. Monk Takes His Medicine' — shares Monk's body and brain yet is not held responsible, and Stanley Tucci's method actor in 'Mr. Monk and the Actor' shows that copying Monk's looks and behavior does not transfer identity. Locke's memory theory breaks on the amnesia of 'Mr. Monk Bumps His Head' (Monk becomes roofer 'Jerry') and the blackout in 'Mr. Monk and the Rapper,' and Reid's brave-officer paradox yields contradiction once recovered Monk remembers being both Monk and Jerry. Hume's bundle theory — 'I never can catch myself,' the self as theatre of successive perceptions — grounds psychological continuity's graded identity, but then cult-swayed Monk in 'Mr. Monk Joins a Cult' might count as a different person, making his deprogramming a kind of murder; the chapter closes by rejecting Reid and Butler's 'simple and unassayable' escape, insisting a philosopher, like a detective, must keep theorizing how Monk stays Monk.

samples.book: 043 - The Golden Compass and Philosophy - God Bites the Dust
samples.title: The Golden Compass and Philosophy
samples.relation: Harris and Baer use the Boatman scene ('Pan is me... we'd die') to test criteria of personal identity against the trilogy: Lyra and Will's inference to a thinking third part, the ghost, reenacts Descartes's dualist reasoning about mind-body distinctness, Iorek's lack of a ghost exemplifies the same-body criterion, and Pantalaimon's instant shape-shifting favors the psychological criterion, spelled out through Locke's prince-and-cobbler memory thought experiment and Parfit's psychological connectedness and continuity. They ask whether Lee Scoresby's dissolution into conscious atoms that reunite with Hester's counts as genuine survival, best accommodated by Locke's consciousness criterion or a panpsychist matter criterion, with Chalmers cited as the contemporary defender of conscious matter. The chapter closes with individuation, whether Lyra and Pan are one person or two, applied to a Primal Fear-style multiple-personality murder trial, the hypothetical of Pan killing someone while Lyra is innocent, and living wills in persistent vegetative states.

samples.book: 079 - Frankenstein and Philosophy - The Shocking Truth
samples.title: Frankenstein and Philosophy
samples.relation: Lopez uses the monster - 'one man made out of many' - to stress-test personal identity: brain-swap and amnesia-torture thought experiments first drive us to identify with our memories (the memory-based psychological criterion) and then, when Victor offers to wipe memory before the pain experiments, with our bodies, yielding inconsistent answers. The monster's own testimony - waking confused, prodding fire like an infant, acquiring language by eavesdropping on Safie's lessons, and building his values from scratch out of Paradise Lost and the cottagers - shows he is a genuinely new person rather than whoever once owned his corpse-parts, since we would not say a memory-wiped torture victim ceases to exist. He concludes the monster satisfies the five listed personhood criteria (consciousness, reasoning, self-motivated activity, communication, self-awareness), with identity riding a continuing stream of consciousness running on a body that is, in the end, secondary 'hardware.'

samples.book: 203 - Watchmen and Philosophy - A Rorschach Test
samples.title: P A R T T H R E E
samples.relation: James DiGiovanna uses Dr. Manhattan's origin — disintegration in the intrinsic field chamber and self-reassembly — plus his teleportations to Mars and his split into three simultaneous selves, to run the classic personal identity debates. Descartes's immaterial thinking substance, Hume's mere bundle of perceptions, and Locke's memory theory are tested against a being who remembers in both time directions and rebuilds his body from pure thought ('restructuring myself after the subtraction of my intrinsic field was the first trick I learned'); Parfit's teletransporter, physical and psychological criteria, and fission cases — mirrored in Nagel's split-brain patients — then show ordinary people cannot say whether they would survive teleporting or bisection. The chapter concludes Dr. Manhattan is the only being with fully secure identity, since his consciousness needs neither body nor an unbroken spatiotemporal path and he can encompass several points of view at once.

samples.book: 093 - More Doctor Who and Philosophy - Regeneration Time
samples.title: 10. One Good, Solid Hope—the Impossible Girl
samples.relation: Elsby and Luzecky ask what stays constant across Clara's echoes and argue traditional identity theories fail her: Locke's memory-continuity and same-life account cannot apply because no echo remembers the others, and Plutarch's Ship of Theseus—invoked by the Doctor's broom speech in 'Deep Breath'—rules out bodily continuity, since the echoes have different bodies and minds. Their positive view is that Clara is less a particular than a universal, a 'recipe' or species whose instances share an essence ('the soufflé isn't the soufflé; the soufflé is the recipe'), with the modern-day Clara 'real' as the origin of the echoes. That essence, shown in climbing the ladder to the clouds in 'The Snowmen,' facing the parasite-god with the most important leaf in human history in 'The Rings of Akhaten,' stepping into the Doctor's torn timeline in 'The Name of the Doctor,' and persuading the Time Lords in 'The Time of the Doctor,' is hope itself.

samples.book: 074 - Planet of the Apes and Philosophy - Great Apes Think Alike
samples.title: Planet of the Apes and Philosophy
samples.relation: Bernard Rollin reads Dr. Zaius's tribunal as 'scientific ideology' in action - 'human see, human do' refuses to believe its own eyes, just as bishops refused to look through Galileo's telescope. He traces the ideology from Newton's 'hypotheses non fingo' through logical positivism's verifiability criterion (which validates the Hasslein Curve prediction while rendering 'there are intelligent beings in Heaven' meaningless) and Wittgenstein's point that 'killing is wrong' is not a fact of the universe, to the 'science is value-free' dogma that left animal pain untested and untreated - as he documents from his own campaign: the empty analgesic literature search, the 1985 federal legislation, and the pain physiologist whose dog research refutes his own denial. Zira's neurosurgery on mute humans repeats what Descartes's beast-machine doctrine licensed, and IASP's language requirement for pain collapses into a Cratylus-grade confusion of necessary and sufficient conditions ('You can't step into the same river once').

samples.book: 027 - Hitchcock and Philosophy - Dial M for Metaphysics
samples.title: Vertigo and Epistemological Vertigo
samples.relation: Flory reads Vertigo as an epistemological parable: Scottie's 'hardheaded Scot' method, collecting facts and deducing from universal principles, fails three times (the step-stool 'cure' for his acrophobia, explaining away Madeleine's 'possession' with the horse statue, forcing Judy up the bell tower for confirmation), delivering an implicit critique of Vienna Circle positivism in the manner of Carnap and Ayer. Against Scottie, the chapter mobilizes Kuhn's theory-laden facts, Aristotle's point that human conduct resists codification by exceptionless laws, and Hume's 'slave of the passions,' with Descartes's automata and Chalmers's philosophical zombies framing the problem of other minds. Midge, who knows people emotionally as well as factually, models the alternative: philosophers who fear 'epistemological vertigo' should give up epistemological training wheels and accept that minds, especially emotions, escape law-like rules.

samples.book: 008 - Woody Allen and Philosophy - You Mean My Whole Fallacy Is Wrong_
samples.title: The Dangers of Hedonism
samples.relation: Sander Lee reads A Midsummer Night's Sex Comedy as Allen's warning against hedonism, tracing that ethos to empiricist thought from Hobbes and Locke through Bentham's utilitarianism to American pragmatism, embodied in Leopold Sturgis, an Ayer-style positivist philosopher who denies everything unprovable yet dies of passion with Dulcy and is deified by Andrew's spirit ball as pagan 'pure essence'. Using Sartre's Nausea, the chapter shows Andrew and Ariel's attempt to recreate their lost 'perfect moment' by the brook failing on every count, proving such moments inauthentic fantasies that ignore freedom, responsibility, and the passage of time. Through Bazin's Nietzschean reading of Renoir (Apollonian order versus Dionysian impulse), it argues that unlike Isaac Davis in Manhattan, the film's characters end more committed to hedonism than they began, with no character left qualified to condemn it.

samples.book: 024 - Bullshit and Philosophy - Guaranteed to Get Perfect Results Every Time
samples.title: Bullshit and Philosophy
samples.relation: 'The Dream of a Bullshit-Free Culture' argues Frankfurt revives a centuries-old philosophical tradition: Socrates searching for genuinely wise people rather than purveyors of hearsay, Descartes' Meditations discarding every belief short of certainty, and Hume's forkcondemning divinity-school metaphysics that contains neither abstract nor experimental reasoning to the flames. The twentieth-century apotheosis is the Vienna Circle, whose Rudolf Carnap dissected Heidegger's 'Das Nichts selbst nichtet' as mere appearance of meaning, calling metaphysicians 'musicians without musical ability'. The editors cast Frankfurt as the latest carrier of this Enlightenment anti-bullshit torch, with the book's popularity reconnecting seminar-room philosophy to the marketplace and voting booth.

samples.book: 015 - The Chronicles of Narnia and Philosophy - The Lion, the Witch, and the Worldview
samples.title: The Chronicles of Narnia and Philosophy
samples.relation: Stephen Webb argues that Lewis gives hearing, not sight, the fundamental role in knowledge: the Dufflepuds choose invisibility over ugliness, the crew in the Dark Island hear nightmares they cannot see, and in The Magician's Nephew Aslan is heard singing before he is seen. Against A.J. Ayer's logical positivism, Webb develops a 'vocative philosophy of sound' in which meaning lives in voices: Jadis's destructive Deplorable Word versus Aslan's world-creating song, Uncle Andrew's tone-deafness to warranted authority, and Shasta in The Horse and His Boy learning who he is from the voice in the dark that answers 'Myself.'

samples.book: 049 - Zombies, Vampires, and Philosophy - New Life for the Undead
samples.title: Possibilities for Human-Vampire Co-operation
samples.relation: Douglas Glen Whitman uses Buffy's vampire brothel (humans paying vampires to feed on willing victims, as Giles concedes) and Blade's mandatory blood bank as two models of human-vampire coexistence to stage the clash between libertarianism (Nozick, Lomasky, Schmidtz) and welfarism (Singer, Unger, G.A. Cohen). He runs vampire personhood through Nozick's criteria from Anarchy, State, and Utopia — sentience, self-consciousness, rationality, free will, moral personality, soul — and argues no standard includes humans while excluding vampires, applying Singer's equal-consideration-of-suffering principle across kinds of beings. He then extends Singer's obligation-to-aid reasoning (rescuing a drowning child vs. donating to UNICEF) to show welfarism would mandate forced blood transfers or 'blood stamps', and argues via Adam Smith's Poor Law settlement rules and modern welfare-based anti-immigration politics that the burden of supporting dependents breeds exclusion. Only the libertarian brothel model of voluntary exchange, he concludes, turns vampire-human relations into a positive-sum game in which humans would actually come to recognize vampires as persons.

samples.book: 022 - The Undead and Philosophy - Chicken Soup for the Soulless
samples.title: Possibilities for Human-Vampire Co-operation
samples.relation: Douglas Glen Whitman contrasts two pop-culture templates: Buffy's vampire brothel, where willing humans pay vampires for consensual bites (Giles calls the customers 'willing victims'), and Blade's implied government blood bank, where humans are forced to donate. Running Robert Nozick's personhood criteria (sentience, rationality, free will, moral agency, soul) against vampires, he argues no standard admits humans while excluding them, so staking vampires violates rights and, on Singer's suffering-equals-suffering logic, refusing consideration is a kind of speciesism. The welfarist side - Singer and Unger's principle that we must prevent bad at little cost, as in the drowning child - would mandate Blade-style forced blood transfers, but Whitman contends such coercion breeds the very xenophobia (Adam Smith's Poor Law settlement rules, anti-immigrant welfare politics) that blocks recognizing vampire personhood. Only a libertarian market of voluntary exchange turns human-vampire relations from a zero-sum war into a positive-sum commerce.

samples.book: 167 - The Ultimate Harry Potter and Philosophy - Hogwarts for Muggles
samples.title: Barton’s Libertarian Interpretation of the Potter Series
samples.relation: The chapter rebuts Prinzi's three arguments one by one: Dumbledore's distrust of power (cauldron-thickness regulations, Buckbeak's condemnation, Harry's underage-magic trial) does not make him libertarian, since Lord Acton's 'power corrupts' is accepted across political theories including America's checks and balances; his gradual, consent-respecting approach to freeing house-elves and his defense of despised minorities (the last giants, Hagrid, Lupin, Firenze) value liberty but not the distinctively robust libertarian right, which, as Locke's point about the civil magistrate and the 'care of souls' shows, also forbids paternalism and punishing victimless vices. Finally, Dumbledore's hands-off headmastership, letting Snape humiliate Neville and staying distant from Harry's battles, is not libertarian policy at all: even a libertarian official must protect people under his authority from abuse, schools are not states, and the state has no business inculcating the self-reliance Dumbledore wants his students to develop.

samples.book: 148 - Black Mirror and Philosophy - Dark Reflections
samples.title: A White Christmas with Dark Reflections
samples.relation: The chapter follows White Christmas's three escalating uses of the Z-eye digital block — Beth blocking Joe (whose information deprivation leads to two deaths), court-ordered blocks extending to children, and Matthew's society-wide red-blur sex-offender block — as a conflict between privacy and access to information. Utilitarian and Kantian frameworks (autonomy, persons as ends) leave the trade-offs genuinely unsettled, while Nozick's minimal state shows the automatic, loophole-free blocking regime is an indefensibly paternalistic state violating proportionality. Arendt's account of meaningfulness through speech grounds the conclusion that erasing someone's face and voice violates their humanity, and the chapter's final move is defamiliarization: if digital blocks are wrong, we should re-examine the social-media blocking, restraining orders, prisons, and sex-offender registries they mirror.

samples.book: 121 - The Twilight Zone and Philosophy - A Dangerous Dimension to Visit
samples.title: 21. That Unnamed Zone We Call Freedom
samples.relation: Hooke reads Serling's ambivalence toward the State through 'The Obsolete Man,' where librarian Romney Wordsworth is condemned as obsolete and reads Psalm 23 to mock the Chancellor — analyzed via Foucault's shepherd-flock model of power and its paradox, which 'The Shelter' restages as neighbors deciding who gets inside. He then maps the Rawls–Nozick dispute: whether a state just enough to enforce equal rights and the difference principle must inevitably invade personal freedom (Nozick's Jerry West self-respect example), with both agreeing that no state squashing dignity and freedom is just. Under a Nietzsche epigraph on the gods' laughter, Wordsworth's smile before death becomes the indefinable freedom of laughing at obsolete authority — the unnamed Zone, running from Socrates and Heraclitus to Serling.

samples.book: 127 - Blade Runner 2049 and Philosophy - This Breaks the World
samples.title: 24. A Modern utopia
samples.relation: Robin Bunce reads 2049 as a libertarian utopia realized: a Los Angeles without welfare, planning, or federal power, where Hayek's market knowledge and Nozick's minimal state have won and everything from water to children to replicants is voluntarily bought and sold. Yet the result is a slave state, and Nozick's freedom-as-non-coercion — the negative liberty Berlin also held — cannot explain Luv, the film's most privileged character, who is nonetheless a slave because her existence hangs wholly on Wallace's will. Quentin Skinner's and Algernon Sidney's neo-Roman liberty, independence from another's will, explains her fear, and the Baseline, like Orwell's 'Thou Art', reveals an ambition to enslave not actions but souls; Freysa's 'we are our own masters' is a republican declaration of independence.

samples.book: 009 - Harry Potter and Philosophy - If Aristotle Ran Hogwarts
samples.title: Barton’s Libertarian Interpretation of the Potter Series
samples.relation: The authors rebut Prinzi's three arguments that Dumbledore is libertarian-minded. Distrust of political power (the Ministry's suspension of Dumbledore, Buckbeak's condemnation, Harry's underage-magic trial) is a non sequitur since non-libertarians limit power through checks and balances too; his defense of house-elves, the giants, and despised-minority teachers like Hagrid, Lupin, and Firenze shows a devotion to liberty liberals share, not the libertarian's distinctively robust right (no paternalism, no victimless-crime laws, no redistribution); and his hands-off management - letting Snape bully Neville, standing apart from Harry's fights - cannot transfer from school to state, and even a libertarian headmaster would be obligated to stop teacher abuse and require professors to teach.

samples.book: 200 - Twilight and Philosophy - Vampires, Vegetarians, and the Pursuit of Immortality
samples.title: 21. That Unnamed Zone We Call Freedom
samples.relation: Hooke stages the liberalism-versus-libertarianism dispute through Serling's ambivalence about the State: Foucault's shepherd-flock model from his Security, Territory, Population lectures fails as politics, since 'The Shelter' shows the shepherd deciding who stays and who goes ends in mob violence, and in 'The Obsolete Man' librarian Romney Wordsworth reads Psalm 23 to a State that has declared God and books obsolete. The Rawls-Nozick quarrel (justice as fairness and the difference principle against Nozick's minimal state and his basketball-shooter case for keeping self-respect out of politics) frames how much State freedom requires. Wordsworth's laugh before his execution, under Nietzsche's epigraph about gods who mock, embodies the undefinable freedom no State can name.

samples.book: 050 - Facebook and Philosophy - What's on Your Mind_
samples.title: index
samples.relation: Fairweather and Halpern defend status updates against the vanity charge using Hume's 'natural sympathy': ambient awareness of hundreds of News Feed lives exercises the fellow-feeling from which Humean moral standards grow, and Facebook's non-overlapping friend lists remove the dominance hierarchies of face-to-face groups. Butera uses Baudrillard's promiscuous 'ecstasy of communication' to read friending as gatekeeper, the status update as moderator of an avatar-self, and the News Feed as a synthesizer that lets users censor encounters, asking with Kierkegaard whether this control forecloses the openness to interruption that makes life meaningful. Doyle and Fraser stage Foucault against Habermas over the MI6 chief's wife's exposed profile, Facebook's Beacon advertising surveillance, and Iran's Twitter revolution: the same diffuse, productive power that lets citizens watch institutions back makes narcissistic self-disclosure ever more available for categorization and control. Bar-Tura's account of organizing Jewish-Muslim teen bowling nights tests Habermas's ideal speech situation and concludes that wall-to-wall interaction must become face-to-face meetings to build real solidarity.

samples.book: 030 - Pink Floyd and Philosophy - Careful with that Axiom, Eugene!
samples.title: Art, Madness, and Syd Barrett
samples.relation: George Reisch reads The Wall through Foucault's Madness and Civilization: madness is not a brain lesion but a historical construction — Renaissance unreason, classical confinement, then Tuke's and Pinel's psychiatric regime in which the madman must know 'he is watched, judged, and condemned' until judgment is internalized — which explains why Pink imprisons himself brick by brick and asks at 'The Trial', 'Have I been guilty all this time?' The fascist worms and skinhead riots of 'Waiting for the Worms' are the same crusade for uniformity that drove Pink mad — Foucault's 'moral city' where 'virtue is an affair of the state' — so fascism and insanity are versions of each other, with Sartre's 'Hell is other people' from No Exit as the framing thought. Both the album ('Outside the Wall': 'the bleeding hearts and artists make their stand') and Foucault end by defending art as the last channel of unreason, and Reisch argues Syd Barrett's unanswerable absence was exactly that interrupting void powering 'Echoes', Dark Side, Wish You Were Here, and The Final Cut.

samples.book: 148 - Black Mirror and Philosophy - Dark Reflections
samples.title: Heaven is a Place on Earth
samples.relation: The chapter argues Black Mirror's perception tech works because the brain constructs experience top-down (predictive coding), so implants like Playtest's mushroom, Arkangel's filter, and Men Against Fire's MASS can inject perceptions and suppress error signals - and Cooper's total VR illusion defeats every one of Descartes's strategies (memory continuity, cross-checking the senses, reason) for telling dream from reality, killing him seconds after implantation. Nozick's experience machine illuminates Danny's preference for Striking Vipers X over his marriage and Arkangel's lesson that filtering Sara's childhood perceptions left her unable to read danger or emotion. Foucault's panopticon (via Bentham) frames White Christmas's cookie interrogation modeled on real police deception (Frazier v. Cupp), the MASS implant's manufacture of 'roach' targets for killing, and Nosedive's self-imposed social ratings as modern perceptual discipline - with only trusted others (Catarina, Susan, Kelly) punching through the manipulation.

samples.book: 236 - The Philosophy of War Films
samples.title: Beyond Panopticism The Biopolitical Labor of Surveillance and War in Contemporary Film
samples.relation: Gooch argues that the post-2005 surveillance film cycle moves 'beyond panopticism': Foucault's disciplinary gaze gives way to Deleuze's 'societies of control,' and the surveiling gaze becomes direct domination and a form of biopolitical labor (Hardt and Negri) rather than an impersonal structure. He reads the prestige dramas (Redacted, Stop-Loss, In the Valley of Elah, Lions for Lambs) as exposing the soldier's proletarianization and self-surveillance, and the thrillers/blockbusters (Déjà Vu, The Kingdom, Body of Lies, The Bourne Ultimatum, Eagle Eye, Burn after Reading) as staging a Marxist antagonism between living labor (the watching hero) and the fixed capital of surveillance technology. Using Deleuze's 'degraded time-image,' Kant's needed separation of subject and law, and Benjamin/Agamben's state of exception, he shows Eagle Eye inverting law and subject to justify preemptive war and turn biopolitical labor into the labor of subjection.

samples.book: 066 - Neil Gaiman and Philosophy - Gods Gone Wild!
samples.title: Neil Gaiman and Philosophy
samples.relation: Najwa Al-Tabaa reads Sandman: Season of Mists through Derrida's paradox that only the unforgivable can truly be forgiven: Morpheus's freeing of Nada works as forgiveness precisely because condemning his lover to Hell was unforgivable, while Lucifer, who was never wronged by the damned, can give them only a devalued semblance of pardon, and they cling to punishment they feel they deserve. She then brings in Foucault's Discipline and Punish and Bentham's Panopticon to read the angels' rebuilt Hell of redemption as the modern rehabilitative prison, where watched souls are expected to reform themselves. The experiment fails, she argues, because redemption is imposed without hearing the prisoners, violating Derrida's condition that forgiveness needs a shared language, so the inmates prefer Lucifer's honest eternity of despair to a salvation they never asked for, a lesson about real prisons that seek rehabilitation through punishment.

samples.book: 184 - The Office and Philosophy - Scenes from the Unexamined Life
samples.title: The Office and Philosophy
samples.relation: Applies Sartre's Being and Nothingness to the mockumentary: Pam's bad faith consists in pretending she has no choice between Jim and Roy (her garbled 'I'm not into Jim' conversation with Karen in 'Ben Franklin'), while the camera's Look - Sartre's keyhole peeper caught in the hallway - turns her into an object not of her making when she is caught watching Jim and Karen in 'The Merger', and her shame finally lets her own her feelings. David Brent's pride (posing with his Inside Paper magazine cover) tries to control the Other's look and fails, since the freely respected gaze he craves cannot be extracted; and the ever-possible camera functions as Foucault's panopticon (Bentham's prison design), visible and unverifiable, silencing Jan on speakerphone in 'Cocktails' and forcing Dwight and Angela's 'Don't linger. Break left' choreography, which makes the viewer a complicit co-worker.

samples.book: 164 - The Girl with the Dragon Tattoo and Philosophy - Everything Is Fire
samples.title: The Girl with the Dragon Tattoo and Philosophy
samples.relation: The chapter uses Foucault to explain how Salander could leave school without a certificate yet master Fermat-class mathematics: schools 'cut' students into fabricated 'human kinds'—the problem-solving child and the at-risk child (Popkewitz's alchemy)—and under No Child Left Behind that sorting licenses surveillance and discipline of everything an at-risk student does. Lisbeth's case shows the machinery: her correct answer marked wrong from the textbook key, her Rubik's-cube brilliance ignored, her 381 days strapped to a bed under Teleborian's silhouette-like gaze recasting Bentham's Panopticon, and her subsequent guardianship extending the watch over her money and behavior. Because power 'produces reality,' the at-risk label becomes self-fulfilling, and Lisbeth's refusal to be disciplined—her silence, tattoos, and asocial style—only supplies fresh evidence for the label.

samples.book: 172 - The Hunger Games and Philosophy - A Critique of Pure Treason
samples.title: The Hunger Games and Philosophy
samples.relation: Van Dyke uses Foucault's account of discipline and 'docile bodies' (with Susan Bordo's feminist elaboration) to explain how the Capitol rules: citizens satiated with abundance channel their hungers into fashion, body modification, and self-surveillance, and this self-focused discipline trains their attention away from the injustices that sustain them — which is how the genuinely affectionate prep team can weep over Katniss yet love the Games. She shows that District 13 disciplines just as totally through rigid schedules, rations, and punishment (the prep team chained for taking bread), so neither Snow's hidden indulgence nor Coin's overt regimentation leaves room for autonomy. Cinna's styling of Katniss demonstrates the alternative: body modification as internally generated self-expression and resistance that helps Katniss become the Mockingjay rather than a docile body.

samples.book: 042 - Supervillains and Philosophy - Sometimes, Evil Is Its Own Reward
samples.relation: Four 'Phase Five' puzzle essays. Lindahl-Urben and Taliaferro use Secret Wars to test omnipotence: the Beyonder, Doom, and Galactus cannot do the logically impossible (no spherical cubes, no stone too heavy to lift), two omnipotent beings collide, and a truly omnipotent being has no desires - so villains can never climb to the top they crave. Matthewson and Wall use Frankfurt cases and reasons-responsive source compatibilism to explain why Eddie Brock is responsible for Venom's villainy (he voluntarily bonded and endorses the symbiote's adjusted psychology) while Anne Weying, horrified by what the symbiote made her do, bears only minimal blame. Pickavance reconstructs the Ship of Theseus with Sandman's 'mansand': combining part exchange with materialism lets Norman Osborn reassemble a duplicate Sandman from his scattered remains, and since neither principle nor soul-dualism comes free, personal identity through material change remains unsolved. Loader argues Brainiac's reinvention as a 'facts and logic' computer embodies disembodied Cartesian AI, so the frame problem (Dennett's exploding robots) and embodied cognition (Clark's Tetris, Dreyfus) suggest his detachment from body and world would make him less, not more, intelligent than the humans he scorns.

samples.book: 160 - Fallout and Philosophy - Thinking Outside the Shelter
samples.title: Notes
samples.relation: David Lawrence opens with Fallout 4's 'Blind Betrayal', where Elder Maxson orders the player to execute Paladin Danse once his synth origin is revealed, and argues that moral status is a matter of capacities - sense of self, notion of past and future, values, life-plans, moral agency - drawing on Charles Taylor's concept of a person and narrative identity, not on biological substrate. Nick Valentine's hunt for Eddie Winter in 'Long Time Coming' and Curie's chosen embodiment in 'Emergent Behavior' show machines weaving reconstructed pasts into new life-plans, while ghouls like Hancock and Raul ('Old School Ghoul') and super mutants like Fawkes (who refuses to enter the lethal radiation chamber: 'I would not rob you of that') and the community-builder Marcus prove branded monsters can be more human than human. The factions embody warring philosophies of moral status: the Institute's property-slavery of its creations, the Brotherhood's 'wisdom of repugnance' (Leon Kass), and the Railroad's capacity-based abolitionism, with DiMA's Far Harbor question - how do you know you are not a synth? - turning the issue on the player.

samples.book: 157 - Dungeons and Dragons and Philosophy - Read and Gain Advantage on All Wisdom Checks
samples.title: Dungeons and Dragons and Philosophy
samples.relation: Silcox and Cox read D&D modules as thought experiments in James Robert Brown's 'laboratory of the mind'. The Tomb of Horrors' four overlapping plane-shifted buildings restate Parfit's teletransporter puzzle — did the character who stepped through get annihilated, or is an exact copy walking around elsewhere, and does the answer differ for a Warforged or Tiefling? — while the Eberron setting's magically sentient Warforged run into Nagel's 'What Is It Like to Be a Bat?': players cannot access Warforged experience and are really exploring what it is like for a human to suspend disbelief, like Greek actors donning masks. Mary Anne Warren's Space Traveler criteria for alien personhood collapse on contact with orcs who pass them yet eat you, and with the Flumph — lawful good, rational, but killed on sight by the authors' own party — showing personhood cannot be the only criterion for how to treat strangers; the closing twist is that philosophy contemplates scenarios sub specie aeternitatis while D&D forces immersion sub specie temporis, a habit of entertaining the impossible that is itself a philosophical virtue.
