samples.title: A Dilemma
samples.relation: The chapter asks 'Is your cookie you?', running theories of personal identity through Black Mirror's copies: the soul theory surfaces when Clayton signs away his 'digital self'; Locke's memory theory implies Cookie-Greta is Greta - a reductio, since one person cannot be wholly in two places at once (the same problem for Ashley Too and the thousand Hang the DJ simulations) - and the perdurantist patch recasts Greta and her cookie as time-slices of one four-dimensional person. Physical theories (Olson's animalism, Unger's brain-essentialism) rule out survival by upload, so Yorkie dies when her body dies even though digital Yorkie continues in San Junipero; Parfit's no-self bundle view and the teletransporter case then dissolve the fear, since there is no ego to lose and ordinary survival is 'about as bad' as being destroyed and replaced by a replica. The upshot: the punishment and immortality plots (Joe's million-year Christmas loop, San Junipero) require cookies to be both conscious and psychologically connected in the right way, and the episodes' horror depends on leaving that genuinely uncertain.

samples.book: 046 - Mr. Monk and Philosophy - The Curious Case of the Defective Detective
samples.title: Mr. Monk Is Mr. Monk
samples.relation: Malloy runs the classic theories of personal identity through Monk episodes. Bodily (really brain) identity fails when 'the Monk' — the reckless medicated alter of 'Mr. Monk Takes His Medicine' — shares Monk's body and brain yet is not held responsible, and Stanley Tucci's method actor in 'Mr. Monk and the Actor' shows that copying Monk's looks and behavior does not transfer identity. Locke's memory theory breaks on the amnesia of 'Mr. Monk Bumps His Head' (Monk becomes roofer 'Jerry') and the blackout in 'Mr. Monk and the Rapper,' and Reid's brave-officer paradox yields contradiction once recovered Monk remembers being both Monk and Jerry. Hume's bundle theory — 'I never can catch myself,' the self as theatre of successive perceptions — grounds psychological continuity's graded identity, but then cult-swayed Monk in 'Mr. Monk Joins a Cult' might count as a different person, making his deprogramming a kind of murder; the chapter closes by rejecting Reid and Butler's 'simple and unassayable' escape, insisting a philosopher, like a detective, must keep theorizing how Monk stays Monk.

samples.book: 058 - Dexter and Philosophy - Mind over Spatter
samples.title: A Story in Search of a Narrator
samples.relation: Brian Gregor reads Dexter through Charles Taylor's 'self-interpreting animal': Dexter's identity is not a fixed thing but comes into being through self-interpretation within an inescapable framework of value, so even his 'Am I good? Am I evil?' rebellion and the Nietzschean Übermensch reading fail to escape the deeper convictions about innocence, evil and desert that Harry's Code presupposes - as his guilt over the innocent Farrow shows. The chapter interprets Dexter's serial failures at being 'seen' - Harry's 'only one who really saw me', Brian's fraternal 'you can be yourself with me', Lila's probing, and Miguel Prado as Aristotle's friend, 'another self' - as Hegelian struggles for recognition that collapse because his real self can never come into the open. Finally, drawing on MacIntyre's narrative account of identity, it argues Dexter is literally a story in search of a narrator, whose selfhood persists through flashbacks, blood slides and noir-style voice-overs, and whose humanity shows in the need to have his account of himself heard and corrected by another.

samples.book: 047 - Anime and Philosophy - Wide Eyed Wonder
samples.title: Is Everybody Disembodied (or, Have We Always Been Posthuman Beings )
samples.relation: Stevens uses the film's closing voice-over 'I am Tetsuo' in Otomo's Akira to run the classic identity-and-mind problems: Heraclitus's river and Plutarch's Ship of Theseus ask whether the grotesquely transformed, Akira-absorbed Tetsuo is still the same person, while Descartes's cogito — riffed as 'cogito ergo Tetsuo' — Turing's Test, and Searle's Chinese Room test whether a voice that seems to think proves a thinker behind it (syntax is not yet shown sufficient for semantics, though Edwin Hutchins's distributed cognition reads the Room from the inside out). Weighing embodiment (Pinker's brain-makes-mind, Dennett's self as a 'center of narrative gravity') against disembodiment (Akira levelling Neo-Tokyo from nothing but cryogenically stored remains; Tetsuo's matter teleportation), he concludes through the problem of representation — every utterance is re-presented, as in Augustine's guilty tears over Dido — that we always treat semblances of thinkers as thinkers, so we may have always been decentered, re-presented, posthuman beings no different from Tetsuo and Akira.

samples.book: 043 - The Golden Compass and Philosophy - God Bites the Dust
samples.title: The Golden Compass and Philosophy
samples.relation: Harris and Baer use the Boatman scene ('Pan is me... we'd die') to test criteria of personal identity against the trilogy: Lyra and Will's inference to a thinking third part, the ghost, reenacts Descartes's dualist reasoning about mind-body distinctness, Iorek's lack of a ghost exemplifies the same-body criterion, and Pantalaimon's instant shape-shifting favors the psychological criterion, spelled out through Locke's prince-and-cobbler memory thought experiment and Parfit's psychological connectedness and continuity. They ask whether Lee Scoresby's dissolution into conscious atoms that reunite with Hester's counts as genuine survival, best accommodated by Locke's consciousness criterion or a panpsychist matter criterion, with Chalmers cited as the contemporary defender of conscious matter. The chapter closes with individuation, whether Lyra and Pan are one person or two, applied to a Primal Fear-style multiple-personality murder trial, the hypothetical of Pan killing someone while Lyra is innocent, and living wills in persistent vegetative states.

samples.book: 010 - Mel Gibson's Passion and Philosophy - The Cross, the Questions, the Controversy
samples.title: Mel Gibson’s Passion and Philosophy
samples.relation: Bronson argues Gibson's fixation on Jesus's suffering is not a Christian oddity but a deeply Jewish mystical one: using William James's four marks of mystical experience (ineffability, noetic quality, transiency, passivity), he reads the Gethsemane opening, where Jesus crushes Satan's serpent and receives a vision of the Father, as a classic mystical trial in the line of Moses at Sinai, Daniel's chariot-throne vision, Elijah's fiery ascent, John the Baptist, Paul's blinding light, and later the Kabbalah and Hasidic masters whose path to God runs through anguish. The Platonic Socrates of the Symposium and Phaedrus (wisdom arriving through the madness of love) and the medieval agreement of al-Ghazali, Maimonides, and Aquinas that reason cannot reach God frame his philosophy-versus-mysticism contrast, including the film's mother-son floorboard scene as love but not full mystical contact. The added scene where Pilate's wife tells him 'If you will not hear the truth, no one can tell you' shows Gibson siding with the mystical path to truth over Pilate's pragmatic one.

samples.book: 021 - U2 and Philosophy - How to Decipher an Atomic Band
samples.title: U2 and Philosophy
samples.relation: Wrathall's introduction argues U2 is philosophically interesting because its enormous popularity holds up a mirror to what 'we' care about (by Nietzsche's test of how a culture stands toward life) and because the band publicly wrestles with the contradictions of the technological-global economy: unprecedented freedom of choice paired with loss of rooted identity, and distant suffering ('Crumbs from Your Table') that we feel both powerless to fix and responsible for. Its showcase reading treats 'Miracle Drug' as a musical theodicy: Bono's plea 'God, I need your help tonight' is answered by the Edge's guitar and by the Matthew 25:35 refrain, so science and medicine count as works of Christian charity. The piece then frames the volume's essays: Plato's ascent of love in the early songs, Kierkegaardian despair after Achtung Baby, Bono's search for authentic identity, the simulacra of 'Even Better than the Real Thing', being-toward-death in the apocalyptic songs, and the Plato-versus-Aristotle quarrel over music's emotional power.

samples.book: 129 - RuPaul's Drag Race and Philosophy - Sissy That Thought
samples.title: 13. The Origins of Self-Love
samples.relation: Anna Marie Fennell reads RuPaul's 'If you can't love yourself, how in the hell you gonna love somebody else?' through theories of self-love. Erich Fromm's four elements of love and Buddhist non-attachment (Jinkx Monsoon's 'water off a duck's back,' the Season Ten Inner Saboteur characters like Eureka's Eufilthior) ground the claim that self-love precedes healthy love for others. Against Aristophanes' myth in Plato's Symposium - the round beings split by Zeus, forever seeking their other half, retold in Hedwig and the Angry Inch - she sides with Ru: completion comes from within, not from a soulmate. Beauvoir's Ethics of Ambiguity (the sub-man and nihilist archetypes seen in self-sabotaging queens like Nina Bo'Nina Brown) and bell hooks's All About Love with Branden's six pillars of self-esteem map onto winners like Jinkx, Sharon Needles, Violet Chachki, and Bianca Del Rio, whose drag personas show existence preceding essence.

samples.book: 169 - The Hobbit and Philosophy - For When You've Lost Your Dwarves, Your Wizard, and Your Way
samples.title: a7.xhtml
samples.relation: The chapter sets the bloody classical ideal of glory (Homer's kleos, Beowulf, Alexander modeling himself on Achilles) - which Augustine already condemned as libido dominandi - against Plato's alternative of a life aimed at the good, the true and the beautiful. Thorin's last charge at the Battle of Five Armies fits the heroic tradition, but Tolkien's real point is that Bilbo, the 'grocer' who feels the dwarves' treasure-lust yet walks away from it, and who ends by inviting the dwarves to four-o'clock tea instead of a victory feast, shows glory subordinated to domestic beauty and humility. Socrates' question in the Apology - why care so little for wisdom and the soul's improvement while chasing wealth, honor and reputation - is exactly the temptation Bilbo resists, and the Symposium's move from battle to a drinking-party of love-of-beauty mirrors Tolkien's placement of heroism in hobbits rather than warriors.

samples.book: 012 - Star Wars and Philosophy - More Powerful than You Can Possibly Imagine
samples.title: The Force of Love
samples.relation: Lawler identifies Hegel's Absolute Spirit with the Force: Hegel's distillation of religious history - divine nature (the Ewoks worshipping C-3PO), the Roman Empire's transcendent Unhappy Consciousness, and Christianity's Consummate Religion - maps onto the saga's movement, with Anakin's virgin birth, prophecy, fall, and Calvary-like redemption fulfilling the pattern differently from the sinless Savior. The Dark Side is the separate ego asserting 'I' against 'We' (Hobbes's war of all against all culminating in the Emperor), and sin is the belief that one is an isolated individual. Against the Jedi's Stoic detachment (Epictetus), the chapter uses Diotima's ladder of love from Plato's Symposium and Hegel's Faust to argue that only passionate, attached love - Anakin's for Padme and Luke's for his father - descends into darkness and brings the Spirit's balance, so 'the Force is with us.'

samples.book: 155 - Downton Abbey and Philosophy - The Truth Is Neither Here Nor There
samples.title: 24. Climbing the Ladder of Love
samples.relation: Brendan Shea reads Downton's romances through each speech of Plato's Symposium in turn. Phaedrus's love-inspired heroism explains Thomas taking a beating to save Jimmy; Pausanias's contrast of common and heavenly love maps onto Mary learning to work within social rules rather than around them (Pamuk versus Matthew); Eryximachus's orderly love is Carson and Mrs. Hughes's skilled, harmonious running of the house; Aristophanes's severed halves fit Anna and Bates merging their lives through prison and rape; and Agathon's naive praise diagnoses Edith's misdirected pursuit of love. Finally Socrates's ladder of love - desire for immortality ascending from one beautiful beloved to moral beauty itself - is played out by Tom and Sybil, whose romance leads him from chauffeur to estate manager and her from fashionable life to nursing, exactly as the ladder predicts.

samples.book: 048 - The Red Sox and Philosophy - Green Monster Meditations
samples.title: April 6th, 2009
samples.relation: David Roochnik interlaces a loss diary (his daughter's soccer defeat and the Sox's 1998 playoff elimination on the same Saturday, the 2003 Grady Little collapse that gave him chest pain, the 2004 comeback) to argue that losing is an art that teaches what winning cannot. The loser's 'if only' imagination transforms the past, the 'it was only a game' rationalization forces honest reflection about what matters, and shared doom forges Red Sox Nation into a community in a way no Yankees nation could exist, since victors never need to think. He applies Plato's Symposium doctrine of Eros, that to love X is to lack X as Socrates lacks wisdom, to explain why eighty-six years of championship-lack made fandom meaningful, and closes fearing that winning in 2004 and 2007 made the Sox 'normal,' eroding the art of losing that glued the Nation together.

samples.book: 144 - Battlestar Galactica and Philosophy - Knowledge Here Begins Out There
samples.title: Becoming One
samples.relation: The chapter reads Baltar's head-Six and Caprica Six's head-Baltar through the gothic Double and Doppelganger tradition and Dissociative Identity Disorder: Number Six is Baltar's repressed guilt over betraying humanity ('I'm your subconscious frakking with your mind'), letting him escape responsibility for signing execution orders in 'Precipice,' while Gina Six serves as a tangible Double. Plato's Symposium myth of the split self frames Baltar and Six as two halves of one whole, since he cannot function without some version of Six present, physical or hallucinated. The resolution is Aristotle's golden mean from Book Two of the Nicomachean Ethics: like integration therapy for DID, virtue is a balance between extremes rather than eliminating one side, so Baltar and Six's child Hera may embody the balanced union of human and Cylon.

samples.book: 088 - Justified and Philosophy - Shoot First, Think Later
samples.title: Justified and Philosophy
samples.relation: The chapter reads season two's families through Engels's Origin of the Family, Private Property and the State: Mags performs the patriarch's role of accumulating and bequeathing wealth (the Black Pike payout 'sufficient to provide for my kin for generations'), Arlo fails it by hoarding nothing for Raylan, and Ava joins Boyd's crime precisely when he hands her the mine money for her mortgage - a moment the author calls borderline prostitution, as Engels predicts. Hegel's Philosophy of Right, where the family exists for love and for forming free moral beings who must leave it, exposes the Bennetts' failure on both counts, while Aristotle's Politics (the polis is prior to the family) and Plato's Republic (rulers without private families, children raised in common) ground the claim that feuding clans need the state. The Kentucky-fried twist: when government and coal companies treat mountain families as spoil, family is sometimes all you've got.

samples.book: 027 - Hitchcock and Philosophy - Dial M for Metaphysics
samples.title: “Your Heavenly Father Feeds Them”
samples.relation: Calef takes the Tides restaurant scene ('Who are you? What are you?') and Diogenes's plucked rooster versus Plato's 'featherless biped' as a springboard for testing every classic criterion of humanity against the film. Aristotle's rational soul fails because Mrs. Bundy's 'brain pans' reasoning is wrong and some humans cannot reason; Descartes's language test fails because the myna bird can learn to talk while horrified humans go mute; Rousseau's free will fails because the birds behave unpredictably and resist instinct while humans are trapped, caged, and herd-like; Aristotle's political animal and Hobbes's social contract fail because the town's hoods and lawbreakers contrast with birds that flock together across species. Even the appeal to God's favor turns dark, as the drunk quotes scripture while Revelation's birds gather for a supper of human flesh, leaving the film a mirror in which we must examine ourselves.

samples.book: 187 - Sons of Anarchy and Philosophy - Brains Before Bullets
samples.title: Sons of Anarchy and Philosophy
samples.relation: Eberl reads Jax's Season 5 dilemma (Tara's ultimatum to leave SAMCRO or lose his family) through Aristotle's account of virtue as character cultivated by habituation in a polis. SAMCRO nurtures genuine virtues—Opie's selfless loyalty, courage under fire, the club's communal generosity toward Donna and Lyla—alongside vices like Clay's greed and Tig's lust, with the golden mean distinguishing Bobby's critical loyalty from Chuckie's obsequiousness and Juice's rash minefield charge. Fr. Ashby's fight to keep Abel in Belfast away from Jax's cycle of violence, and the contrast between Deputy Chief Hale's law-abiding ideals and Mayor Hale's self-serving development, illustrate Aristotle's claim that legislators and environments make citizens good or bad. The chapter concludes that Jax's very mix of virtue and vice—the 'savage' needed to head the table—may be what reform requires, at moral cost.

samples.book: 036 - The Legend of Zelda and Philosophy - I Link Therefore I Am
samples.title: Paradise Found
samples.relation: Brown reads The Minish Cap's Hyrule as a working utopia: its Royal Family, guards, and market traders loosely realize Plato's Republic classes from Book V onward, but with fluid social boundaries (Zelda wanders the festival unharassed), no slavery, and relaxed state control that Plato's static order lacked. The town matches Aristotle's polis design (walled, defensible, right-sized, river-powered yet self-sufficient), while the surrounding pastoral landscape embodies Kantian disinterested beauty in nature and the Schillerian idea that through beauty we arrive at freedom. Its vague, prophet-free Picori religion of benevolent Christs-in-miniature needs no Kierkegaardian leap of faith, so unlike Hitler's Germany or Stalin's Russia, Hyrule is utopia actually achieved, and explorable, through Link.

samples.book: 107 - Deadpool and Philosophy - My Common Sense Is Tingling
samples.title: 14. I’m an X-Man!
samples.relation: Daniel Alloy argues Deadpool keeps insisting 'I'm an X-Man!' because being a hero is not a private choice but a social standing: with Aristotle's beast-or-god line about those who cannot live in society and Hegel's account of mutual recognition in the Phenomenology of Spirit, he contends Wade needs heroes he recognizes to recognize him as one in return. The Thunderbolts ('the selfish Avengers') and X-Force recruited him as a merc and so could not grant that recognition, and Cable offers approval from superiority rather than recognition between equals—a friendship of utility where Wade wants one of virtue. Only Captain America's Avengers card treats him as an equal, and even that recognition must be completed by the whole hero community before Wade can accept himself as the hero he already is.

samples.book: 142 - The Avengers and Philosophy - Earth's Mightiest Thinkers
samples.title: Neither Gods nor Beasts But Political Animals
samples.relation: Spanakos denies the official line that the Avengers assemble from necessity—Thor beats Loki alone—arguing instead through Aristotle that the team is a polis: heroes join for safety but stay for the good life, since outside the polis one is either a god or a beast. Ms. Marvel's miserable solo run (unrecognized by Stilt-Man, a 'Where Are They Now?' has-been) ends only when she returns to lead the Mighty Avengers among friends who share her arete; the self-loathing Jessica Jones finds eudaimonia through philia with Carol, Luke Cage, and the team that delivers her baby; even the arrogant Hank Pym regains excellence by defending Tony and leading a new team. Even gods like Thor and near-beasts like the Hulk, the chapter concludes, need the Avengers to flourish.

samples.book: 274 - Coffee – Philosophy for Everyone - Grounds for Debate
samples.title: Coffee - Philosophy for Everyone
samples.relation: Sadler argues black coffee, unlike ceremonial tea, is the realist emblem of our anxious, isolated postmodern condition, and that the chain coffeehouse is a 'non-place' of public anonymity that only simulates the sociality we crave. Against Aristotle's confident view of humans as social animals whose eudaimonia presupposes a settled social order, she sets Nietzsche's alienated individual free to create values — then argues Nietzsche errs: using the trivial cappuccino-vs-latte choice, she shows (via Wittgenstein's private-language argument and Korsgaard) that even solitary choices need reasons intelligible to others, so individual choice cannot be self-justifying and our search for meaningful, non-arbitrary lives is irreducibly social.

samples.book: 190 - The Ultimate Star Wars and Philosophy - You Must Unlearn What You Have Learned
samples.title: Notes
samples.relation: Littmann shows Luke, Leia, and Han repeatedly put friends and family above the galaxy's freedom - Luke abandoning Dagobah for Bespin, the Jabba rescue, refusing to kill Vader - in the tradition of Homer's heroes, then submits them to Athenian scrutiny. Socrates's refusal to escape his Athens prison and his implicit just agreement with the city set civic duty over friendship; Plato would abolish the guardians' family and censor the Zeus-Kronos patricide myth yet approves of Luke sparing Vader; Aristotle prizes philia but holds citizens belong to the state. He concludes the philosophers mostly win: heroic loyalty is often moral failure, and good moral reasoning asks how many people an action affects, not just whom you love.

samples.book: 051 - Soccer and Philosophy - Beautiful Thoughts on the Beautiful Game
samples.title: The Good Gossip
samples.relation: Borge weighs Jimmy Sirrel's claim that the best team always wins and the rest is gossip against Alex Ferguson insisting his side played better in a 1–4 defeat to Liverpool, framing the dispute as football Nominalism (only particular matches and results exist) versus football Platonism (an ideal way of playing exists over and above results). He rejects the Platonic ideal as metaphysically impossible—two perfect teams could never both score on every chance while conceding nothing, and style comparisons like catenaccio versus Brazil 1970 collapse without appeal to results—and instead uses possible-worlds counterfactuals: a team can be 'really' best yet unlucky when it creates objective scoring opportunities, like John Terry's slipped 2008 Champions League penalty or Spain's wrongly disallowed golden goal against South Korea in 2002, that go in across the closest possible worlds. Since Liverpool's deeply unfair 2005 comeback in Istanbul is celebrated as a classic, football is fiction and drama rather than a fairness-measuring contest, and the resulting what-if moaning is the good gossip that makes barstool debate worthwhile.

samples.book: 037 - The Wizard of Oz and Philosophy - Wicked Wisdom of the West
samples.title: Getting to Oz
samples.relation: Auxier uses the Wizard's demand that Dorothy kill the Witch to split 'ought' from 'can'—ethics from the metaphysics and logic of possibility—and then asks whether Oz is a genuinely possible world. He explains David Lewis's modal realism (every genuine possibility actual in its own causally isolated world) through counterfactuals about which network aired the film, dissolves the silver-versus-ruby slippers conflict by assigning book-Oz and film-Oz to different possible worlds, and argues that since no flat contradiction can be eked out of the Oz stories, Lewis is committed to Oz's being real—though Maguire's inter-world travel and Elphaba's hybrid, soul-less trans-world identity (her counterpart in our world being, playfully, Dorothy) stretch Lewis's 'counterparts' doctrine to its limit. Peirce supplies the closing caution, with Boole, that logic is a set of norms for how we can and ought to think rather than a proven mirror of other worlds, so believing in Oz's full reality remains permissible fun rather than an obligation.

samples.book: 043 - The Golden Compass and Philosophy - God Bites the Dust
samples.title: The Golden Compass and Philosophy
samples.relation: Auxier tests Pullman's many-worlds premise, setting Asriel's coin-toss explanation and the Barnard-Stokes hypothesis against Book III's claim that unchosen possibilities are 'snuffed out like candles,' then measures the trilogy against David Lewis's causally independent possible worlds, which forbid the subtle knife's transworld travel and leave the chill Lyra feels at the thought of 'another Lyra' in Will's Oxford as an unresolved transworld-identity puzzle. Compiling fourteen kinds of conscious beings from humans and dæmons to specters and the Abyss itself, he argues Pullman's cosmology is panpsychist and aesthetic rather than moral or epistemic, ordered by what the alethiometer, the knife, and the spyglass can and cannot do, with the alethiometer submitting to the knife and love alone able to break it, as Will's love for his mother and for Lyra does twice. Peirce's agapicism, evolution by creative love alongside chance and mechanical necessity, supplies the closest philosophical analogue to Pullman's 'Matter loved Dust.'

samples.book: 301 - Comics as Philosophy
samples.title: index
samples.relation: This composite chapter opens with the volume's Introduction and then runs several essays. Jeff McLaughlin's 'What If?' reads DC's Crisis on Infinite Earths and Marvel's What If? series as literal illustrations of Leibniz's possible-worlds metaphysics: the multiverse of Earth-1, Earth-2 and the 3,000 doomed universes dramatizes counterfactuals and Leibniz's Theodicy argument (via the principle of sufficient reason) that God actualizes only the best of infinitely many possible worlds, with Descartes invoked on why a perfect God permits imperfection. Amy Kiste Nyberg's essay analyzes the 1954 Senate hearings on EC horror comics (Gaines's 'The Orphan') as an applied-ethics clash between publishers' free expression and protecting children, explicitly deploying Mill's On Liberty and harm principle to argue why the child-audience framing defeats the anti-censorship case. Stanford Carpenter's piece treats the Black Captain America (Truth: Red, White, and Black) as an epistemology-of-authorship problem.

samples.book: 093 - More Doctor Who and Philosophy - Regeneration Time
samples.title: 6. Weeping Angels and Many Worlds
samples.relation: Sutton argues the causal loops of 'Blink' and 'The Angels Take Manhattan' need not destroy libertarian free will: the Doctor's claim that a known future is 'written in stone' conflates ordinary foreknowledge, which leaves agents free to make the knower wrong, with infallible knowledge that only exists because the act occurs. Adapting Hugh Everett's many-worlds interpretation of quantum mechanics to free choices, he shows how branching timelines let the Doctor read Melody Malone, decline to break River's wrist, and still close the loop—some parallel Doctor does what the book records—while Aristotle's future contingents in De Interpretatione secure the indeterminacy of what 'will' happen. Answering the objection that branch-splitting is really fatalism, he appeals to the subjective viewpoint (what matters is 'my me'), explains how Kathy and Billy's messages in 'Blink' reach Sally on at least one branch, and solves why the Doctor is always so lucky: we follow the one branch where he survives.

samples.book: 074 - Planet of the Apes and Philosophy - Great Apes Think Alike
samples.title: Planet of the Apes and Philosophy
samples.relation: David Morgan separates the franchise's two kinds of time travel. Forward travel is physically respectable: special-relativistic time dilation (Taylor's six months against nearly 700 Earth years implies 99.99997 percent of light speed) and gravitational dilation near black holes, confirmed daily by muon lifetimes and GPS satellite corrections. Backward travel, as when Cornelius, Zira, and Milo flee the doomsday blast to 1973, invites the Grandfather Paradox - Hasslein killing the apes would erase the future they came from - but the films resolve it through a closed causal loop in which Hasslein's killings set Caesar's rebellion in motion. Morgan then reads the Aldo-versus-Caesar continuity clash between Escape and Conquest through Hasslein's freeway-of-time speech as a multiple-timelines model aligned with the Many Worlds interpretation of quantum mechanics, which also lets fans file the Burton and Rise reboots as parallel-universe futures.

samples.book: 131 - Avengers Infinity Saga and Philosophy - Go for the Head
samples.title: 5. Getting Time Travel Right
samples.relation: Duncan Gale asks whether Endgame 'gets time travel right,' using David Lewis's 'The Paradoxes of Time Travel' to explain personal time versus external time (Steve and Nebula meeting their past selves), causal loops (Tony quoting the saying about money and time back to Howard, who seemingly hears it first), and the grandfather paradox (Rhodey's baby-Thanos plan, which the existence of Nebula proves the Avengers would always fail to carry out). He traces Marvel's branching-timeline rule from Marvel Two-In-One #50 through the Ancient One's warning that removing a stone splits reality, and argues the film's moral is that the Avengers refuse quick resets and dutifully return the stones, while Thanos would shred the universe and rebuild a 'grateful' one. The chapter closes with Ivan Karamazov's challenge about building the edifice of human happiness on a tortured child's tears, which Thanos would accept and the Avengers refuse.

samples.book: 178 - LEGO and Philosophy - Constructing Reality Brick by Brick
samples.title: Notes
samples.relation: Leuenberger argues that a LEGO MOC is a surprisingly faithful model of David Lewis's Humean supervenience: the world is just a vast mosaic of local matters of particular fact — homogeneous, arbitrarily recombinable atomic bricks (fundamental properties at space-time points) with no necessary connections, Hume's 'greater denier', versus gunky Play-Doh or jigsaw pieces. Ockham's Razor motivates the view (while also able to cut against a divine master builder, whom Lewis's world lacks, though LEGO-world builders likewise stand outside their creations), and Lewis's concrete possible worlds make every build a replica rather than a creation, answered to the 'incredulous stare' by quantitative parsimony. Four-dimensionally stacked creations model change as variation along temporal parts, while the causation objection — nothing in one LEGO creation brings about the next — marks the fundamental Humean/non-Humean divide.

samples.book: 112 - The Americans and Philosophy - Reds in the Bed
samples.title: 4 On the Origin of the State
samples.relation: Opening with Newt Gingrich's complaint that students 'don't read enough Locke' and the Chinese premier's appeal to Rousseau, the chapter compares the three contract theorists' states of nature and purposes of government: Hobbes's war of every man against every man yielding an absolute sovereign with no separation of powers, Locke's peaceful nature in which mixing labor with land creates property and money then creates inequality, so that government's 'great and chief end' is protecting property through limited, separated powers and no food stamps, and Rousseau's compassionate natural humans corrupted when the first man enclosed land, so the state was founded on fraud and a general will that should 'force him to be free' and give people food stamps. Smith then reads the actual US founding as a chaste Lockean contract 'bastardized' on race and sex - the Declaration plagiarized from Locke, Abigail Adams's 'remember the ladies' laughed off, Dred Scott, with the 14th Amendment as the de-bastardizing 'Charter of Universal Freedom' - while Engels derives the state historically from the Iroquois and Greek gens, private property and class conflict. A final section documents white supremacy inside the tradition (Kant inventing the scientific concept of race, Hegel and Hume on Black inferiority), John Stuart Mill's 'Negro Question' as the tradition's decisive anti-racist break, Locke's own entanglements with the slave trade, and Marx's condemnation of slavery as super-exploitation.

samples.book: 049 - Zombies, Vampires, and Philosophy - New Life for the Undead
samples.title: No Way Out
samples.relation: Leah Murray argues Romero's Dead films stage the American contest between individualism and communitarianism inside the social contract: in Night of the Living Dead, communitarian Ben barricading the farmhouse against every-man-for-himself Mr. Cooper hiding in the basement; in Dawn of the Dead, the Peter-Roger-Fran-Stephen mall commune collapsing when Stephen's 'it's ours, we took it' meets the bikers; in Day of the Dead, Sarah's compassion against the racist, harassing soldiers; in Land of the Dead, Kaufman's Fiddler's Green as a Hobbesian Leviathan born of fear, complete with bread-and-circuses for the poor. Against the Hobbesian fear-born contract (Dawn opens in a full state-of-nature collapse) she sets Rousseau's general will and Tocqueville's civic association, embodied in Riley's freely formed community and in Big Daddy's zombies, who organize, turn from eating humans, and bring down the Leviathan. The films' verdict: fear-based individualist contracts collapse under their own contradictions, while compassionate cooperation — even among the Undead — is the only way out, even if Romero doubts its ultimate viability.

samples.book: 074 - Planet of the Apes and Philosophy - Great Apes Think Alike
samples.title: Planet of the Apes and Philosophy
samples.relation: Leslie Dale Feldman reads the 1968 film's blasted opening as Hobbes's state of nature - 'solitary, poore, nasty, brutish, and short' - with the Lawgiver's 'Beware the beast Man' scroll echoing Hobbes's three causes of war (competition, fear, glory) and Plato's Ring of Gyges explaining why even the 'just' man acts rightly only under compulsion, both grounding the social contract's origin story. She then casts Dr. Zaius as Alexis de Tocqueville's tyranny of the majority - erasing Taylor's writing, lobotomizing Landon, and sealing Cornelius's cave 'to spare them all the care of thinking' - with Rousseau's man 'born free; and everywhere he is in chains' behind it. samples.title: 6. Weeping Angels and Many Worlds

samples.book: 074 - Planet of the Apes and Philosophy - Great Apes Think Alike
samples.title: Planet of the Apes and Philosophy
samples.relation: Ralph Shain argues forward and backward time travel are categorically different: relativistic time dilation is conceptually harmless (in Boulle's novel Merou could not return to Soror for a thousand years), but Escape from the Planet of the Apes' backward jump is conceptually impossible because it treats the open future as fixed like the past - Hasslein's plan to kill baby Milo is the Grandfather Paradox, checked against presentist, possibilist, and eternalist ontologies of time. The real philosophical engine is Aristotle's sea-battle argument from the law of excluded middle: since Cornelius's story of the takeover is past for the apes and future for 1973 humans, the film's causal loop (Milo saved at the circus) enacts the fatalist conclusion that the ape takeover will necessarily occur. Hasslein's freeway image of time defeats itself - switching lanes means landing in the past of a different, parallel universe, so the apes' jump would be travel between worlds, not times.

samples.relation: Written as a dialogue in which Death visits the sweeper Lu-Tze, the chapter distinguishes Discworld fate—narrativium and narrative causality, where million-to-one chances come off and Mort's attempt to save a princess bounced back into an alternative timeline—from the Roundworld debates about determinism. The Disc's changeable past—Dios traveling back to found Djelibeybi, Rincewind's sandwich seeding life, Vimes in his own past—is what motivates Carneades's distinction between truth and necessity, and the Stoic line that fate can work through the witches' own free choices.

samples.title: Tomorrow Is Yesterday
samples.relation: Uses the Bajoran Prophets, who experience no linear time ('What is this... time?'), to frame a tour of time's metaphysics: Newton's absolute container versus Leibniz's relationism (the incoherence of a 'temporal vacuum'), Augustine's mind-dependent time (illustrated by 'The Inner Light' and O'Brien's implanted prison years in 'Hard Time'), and McTaggart's argument that neither the A-series nor the B-series can account for change, illustrated by Tasha Yar's death in 'Skin of Evil' and Kirk's Liar-paradox victories over Nomad and Norman. The chapter defends the A-series via tense, then weighs presentism — which would make 'Tomorrow Is Yesterday' and 'Trials and Tribble-ations' impossible — against eternalism, whose fatalism Data embraces when his severed head turns up in 'Time's Arrow' ('It has occurred. samples.title: The Ultimate Daily Show and Philosophy
samples.relation: Gettings asks how a self-described fake news show can inform viewers, and answers by defining fiction as non-deceptive make-believe, Stewart's 'hilarious make-'em-ups' (the Rick Santorum quiz), distinct from lies because truth-value and research do not settle the category, as when Colbert's 2003 projection of Bush's reelection accidentally came true but stayed fiction. He identifies the show's cues for separating real from fake: sheer outrageousness (Samantha Bee on North Korean soldiers), the convention of Stewart playing straight man to unreliable 'senior' correspondents (John Oliver's fabricated Truman history, Ed Helms on the John Roberts nomination), and obviously doctored graphics like Jason Jones's Clooney fundraiser photo. samples.book: 066 - Neil Gaiman and Philosophy - Gods Gone Wild!
samples.title: Neil Gaiman and Philosophy
samples.relation: Tuomas Manninen asks how Gaiman's recycled mythological figures can be the same characters as their originals when Revelation's male, sword-wielding War becomes Good Omens' arms-dealing Carmine 'Red' Zuigiber and Pestilence retires in 1936 for Pollution, with the problem of talking truthfully about non-existent entities reaching back to Plato's Sophist. David Lewis's 'Truth in Fiction' makes the original author the arbiter of a character's properties, and Amie Thomasson's artifact theory makes fictional characters abstract artifacts created by authors, but only adding the type/token distinction and Wittgenstein's family resemblances, the same criss-crossing network of overlapping similarities by which we count games, lets Revelation's Four Horsemen and Gaiman's Four Bikers be tokens of one type. He closes with Russell's defense of philosophy's value: like Richard Mayhew's tale of London Below, a philosophical answer need not convince or be final to teach us 'what things may be.'

The upshot: ordinary viewers know exactly what is true in the show (they were smoking dope), while the theories strain to keep up - 'yeah, not so quick.'
